picks.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C-Mutated NSCLC.

sections.objective: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.
sections.results: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; P<0.001). The median overall survival was 17.7 months with divarasib and 12.0 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for death, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.78; P<0.001). Of the 328 patients who could be evaluated for response, a confirmed response occurred in 58.4% in the divarasib group and in 32.3% in the control group. The median duration of response was 11.9 months with divarasib and 6.9 months with control treatment. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

picks.title: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy.

sections.objective: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.
sections.methods: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.
sections.results: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group.
sections.conclusion: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

picks.title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
picks.abstract: Abstract Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence 1,2 . Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly 3,4 . However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin–photon interface—namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes—has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin–photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics 5,6 while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design 7 and processable materials 8–10 .

picks.title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada’s loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study
picks.abstract: Abstract Objective To describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada’s measles elimination status. Design Descriptive analysis of the cohort of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario’s public health surveillance system during the outbreak period: epidemiological week of 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025. Setting Ontario, Canada. Participants Individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during the outbreak period. Exposure Exposure to measles virus associated with the Ontario outbreak and related transmission chains. Main outcome measures Demographic characteristics, vaccination status, admission to hospital, complications, pregnancy associated outcomes, mortality, and evidence of international spread based on measles virus genotyping and sequencing. Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition incorporating epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries. Results The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada’s measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population. Among the 2377 cases, approximately three quarters of cases (n=1736, 73.0%) occurred in individuals aged 19 years or younger, 2121 (89.2%) were unvaccinated, and 97 (4.1%) had unknown vaccination status. The outbreak was associated with 166 (7%) admissions to hospital, 13 ( Conclusions These findings highlight the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscore the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks. This outbreak shows the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of long standing immunity gaps within interconnected communities across the Americas and the population-level protection that limited broader community transmission.

picks.title: A CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation.
picks.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit. Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro-myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

picks.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
sections.methods: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. The data cutoff date was March 23, 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival were evaluated as dual primary endpoints using a graphical multiple-testing approach with prespecified alpha allocation. Progression-free survival was assessed every 8 weeks through to week 56, then every 12 weeks thereafter; overall survival was assessed continuously. The safety analysis included all randomly assigned patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. For progression-free survival, missing radiographic assessments were handled using prespecified censoring rules; no imputation was performed for missing overall survival or safety data. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06132958) and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p<0·0001) and median overall survival was 19·0 months (16·1-not reached) in the sac-TMT group and 12·1 months (11·0-15·2) in the TPC group (0·68 [0·55-0·84]; p=0·0001). 265 (69%) of 384 patients in the sac-TMT group and 210 (57%) of 367 in the TPC group had a grade 3 or higher adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 133 (35%) patients in the sac-TMT group and 117 (32%) patients in the TPC group. Treatment-related adverse events led to death in three (<1%) patients in the sac-TMT group and three (<1%) in the TPC group.
sections.conclusion: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

picks.title: Deep sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes uncovers substantial contribution of rare variants to agronomic traits.
picks.abstract: Rare variants are highly abundant, yet their genome-wide contributions to agronomic traits remain elusive in plants. Here, we performed deep whole-genome sequencing of 3,367 diverse elite maize inbred lines, uncovering 75.3 million variants, of which 79.2% were rare. Overall, we identified 411 independent association signals for 10 agronomic traits, including 359 attributable to globally rare variants, with rare variants showing effect sizes approximately 2.4 times those of common variants. Frequency-stratified genome-based restricted maximum likelihood (GREML) analyses indicated that rare variants captured a substantial proportion of phenotypic variance for traits under strong adaptive selection, consistent with the allele frequencies of trait-associated variants shifting from common in tropical to rare in temperate maize. Complementing conventional variant-level genome-wide association studies (GWAS), gene-based tests identified an additional 94 candidate gene-trait associations. Our study highlights rare variants as important components of the genetic architecture of complex agronomic traits in maize and provides much-needed resources for future functional studies and breeding.

picks.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals.
picks.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°-twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

items.title: Gram-Negative Bacterial Resistance.
items.abstract: The rapid worldwide spread of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria is driven by a complex interplay of human, environmental, and health care-associated factors and accelerated by mobile genetic elements that facilitate the dissemination of resistance genes. Resistance in gram-negative bacteria arises primarily through reduced drug entry, active drug efflux, modification of antibiotic targets, and enzymatic drug inactivation, most notably through β-lactamase production. Clinically important resistant pathogens include extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. Limited access to effective antibiotics and the continued emergence of resistance to available agents pose substantial challenges to the management of these infections. Appropriate management requires timely and accurate diagnostics, targeted use of newer β-lactam agents, effective source control, and judicious selection of treatment durations.

items.title: Tozorakimab to Prevent COPD Exacerbations.

sections.objective: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have exacerbations despite receiving standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. Dysregulated interleukin-33 signaling is implicated in the pathogenesis of COPD. Tozorakimab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the activity of interleukin-33.
sections.methods: In two replicate phase 3 trials (OBERON and TITANIA), we enrolled adults with COPD who were current or former smokers and had a history of exacerbations in the previous year despite receiving stable standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. There were no eligibility criteria related to blood eosinophil count. Patients were randomly assigned to receive add-on subcutaneous tozorakimab (300 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations that occurred over a 52-week period among former smokers, and the first key secondary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations in the overall population. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: The overall population in OBERON included 446 patients in the tozorakimab group and 431 in the placebo group, and in TITANIA included 438 in the tozorakimab group and 435 in the placebo group. The annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations among former smokers was 1.34 events in the tozorakimab group and 1.90 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.88; P = 0.002) in OBERON, and 1.37 events and 2.07 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.80; P<0.001), in TITANIA. In the overall population, the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations was 1.41 events in the tozorakimab group and 2.00 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001) in OBERON, and 1.44 events and 2.03 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.84; P<0.001), in TITANIA. Adverse events occurred in 70.4% of the patients in the tozorakimab group and in 77.2% of those in the placebo group in OBERON, and in 80.1% and 79.8%, respectively, in TITANIA.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with COPD, treatment with tozorakimab resulted in a significantly lower rate of moderate or severe exacerbations than placebo in the cohort of former smokers and in the overall population of current and former smokers. (Funded by AstraZeneca; OBERON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05166889; TITANIA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05158387.).

items.title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope.

sections.objective: In patients with syncope who present to the emergency department for evaluation, diagnosing an underlying cardiac arrhythmia remains difficult.
sections.methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized, controlled trial at 45 hospitals in the United Kingdom to assess the effects of 14-day cardiac monitoring on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes among patients with syncope. Adults with syncope that remained unexplained after an evaluation in the emergency department were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo 14-day ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring (the intervention group) or to receive the standard care provided for patients with unexplained syncope at each participating site (the standard-care group). The primary outcome was the mean number of patient-reported episodes of syncope at 1 year.
sections.results: A total of 2234 patients underwent randomization: 1123 were assigned to the intervention group and 1111 to the standard-care group. The mean age of the patients was 58.3 years, and 52.1% were male. After the exclusion of patients who did not complete any follow-up, a total of 1970 patients (1004 in the intervention group and 966 in the standard-care group) were included in the primary analysis. The mean (±SD) number of patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year was 1.37±5.10 in the intervention group and 1.58±8.56 in the standard-care group (incidence rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 1.18; P = 0.42). A total of 49 adverse events were reported in the intervention group, and 8 adverse events were reported in the standard-care group, with 1 serious adverse event in each group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with syncope that remained unexplained after evaluation in the emergency department, the use of 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring did not result in significantly fewer patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation and National Health Service Research Scotland; ASPIRED ISRCTN Registry number, ISRCTN10278811.).

items.title: Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions: Detection Is No Longer Diagnosis.
items.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

items.title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm.
items.abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

items.title: B cell subsets are associated with durable responses in distinct cancer types after immune checkpoint inhibition.
items.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A-positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

items.title: Stress hyperglycemia impairs FOXK2-dependent macrophage cardiac repair after myocardial infarction.
items.abstract: Stress hyperglycemia (SHG) predicts poor outcomes after myocardial infarction (MI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify FOXK2 as a key regulator of macrophage-mediated cardiac repair. FOXK2 expression was reduced in cardiac macrophages from hyperglycemic mice after MI and in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients with MI with SHG, whereas macrophage-specific FOXK2 deficiency aggravated cardiac injury. Under high-glucose conditions, FOXK2 was glycosylated at T552 by O-GlcNAc transferase, promoting its ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation. Mass spectrometry and functional assays showed that the FOXK2T552A variant resisted hyperglycemia-induced degradation. Integrated CUT&Tag and RNA-seq analyses revealed that FOXK2 restrained pro-inflammatory cytokine expression by suppressing H3K27 acetylation. Thus, our findings identify FOXK2 as a critical regulator that supports cardiac repair during hyperglycemia, and targeting excessive FOXK2 O-GlcNAcylation may offer a therapeutic strategy for patients with MI and SHG.

items.title: T cell-mediated depletion of intratumoral regulatory T cells using a CCR8xCD3 T cell-engaging bispecific antibody (TCB) promotes antitumor immunity in preclinical mouse models.
items.abstract: T cell-engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (Treg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. Treg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-mediated Treg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing Treg cells in a T cell-mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral Treg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti-PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of Treg cells.

items.title: In Vitro Fertilization or Intrauterine Insemination in Unexplained Infertility.

sections.objective: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points.
sections.results: A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation.
sections.conclusion: In couples with unexplained infertility, treatment with four cycles of IUI with ovarian stimulation was not noninferior to treatment with one complete cycle of IVF with respect to the cumulative live-birth rate. (Funded by the Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; FIIX Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry number, ACTRN12619001003167.).

items.title: Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To compare the clinical effectiveness of three splints after repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons: forearm based (long), Manchester short (short), and relative motion flexion (mini) splints.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomised, parallel group, pragmatic, superiority, clinical trial. 430 participants (aged ≥16 years) requiring rehabilitation after primary repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons in one or two fingers of the hand according to British Society for Surgery of the Hand guidelines. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to the long, short, or mini splint. Splints were worn continuously for five weeks and intermittently for a further week at night and in vulnerable situations such as public environments. Masking participants was not possible owing to the nature of the intervention.
sections.results: 430 participants were randomised to the long splint (n=143), short splint (n=140), or mini splint (n=147) and 403 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Adherence, defined as wearing the splint for a minimum of five weeks, was 83% (118/143) for the long splint, 76% (106/140) for the short splint, and 78% (115/147) for the mini splint. Mean post-randomisation PRWHE scores were 24.5 (standard deviation 15.5) in the long splint group, 23.5 (16.7) in the short splint group, and 22.4 (15.0) in the mini splint group, with adjusted between group differences of 0.3 (98.3% confidence interval -4.0 to 4.6, P=0.88) for the long versus short splint, 2.3 (-1.9 to 6.5, P=0.19) for the long versus mini splint, and 2.0 (-2.2 to 6.3, P=0.25) for the short versus mini splint. Serious adverse event rates occurred in 10% (14/143) of participants in the long splint group, 11% (15/140) in the short splint group, and 11% (16/147) in the mini splint group.
sections.conclusion: This trial found no statistically significant difference in clinical effectiveness between the long, short, and mini splint. Apart from some small differences, secondary outcomes were comparable across all three groups.
sections.other: 26 UK hospitals. The primary outcome was the mean post-randomisation score on the patient-rated wrist and hand evaluation (PRWHE) instrument at 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks, analysed by intention to treat.

items.title: Deep sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes uncovers substantial contribution of rare variants to agronomic traits.
items.abstract: Rare variants are highly abundant, yet their genome-wide contributions to agronomic traits remain elusive in plants. Here, we performed deep whole-genome sequencing of 3,367 diverse elite maize inbred lines, uncovering 75.3 million variants, of which 79.2% were rare. Overall, we identified 411 independent association signals for 10 agronomic traits, including 359 attributable to globally rare variants, with rare variants showing effect sizes approximately 2.4 times those of common variants. Frequency-stratified genome-based restricted maximum likelihood (GREML) analyses indicated that rare variants captured a substantial proportion of phenotypic variance for traits under strong adaptive selection, consistent with the allele frequencies of trait-associated variants shifting from common in tropical to rare in temperate maize. Complementing conventional variant-level genome-wide association studies (GWAS), gene-based tests identified an additional 94 candidate gene-trait associations. Our study highlights rare variants as important components of the genetic architecture of complex agronomic traits in maize and provides much-needed resources for future functional studies and breeding.

items.title: Minimally Invasive Management of Cardiac Tamponade Complicating Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Technical Note.

sections.objective: Cardiac tamponade is an uncommon but potentially catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), particularly when caused by iatrogenic hemopericardium, with high mortality among patients requiring emergency cardiac surgery. We describe a structured minimally invasive subxiphoid protocol modification for immediate intraprocedural tamponade management and place this experience in the context of current evidence.
sections.methods: Between January 2023 and April 2026, cardiac tamponade developed intra- or peri-procedurally in 4 consecutive patients among approximately 350 TAVI procedures at a single tertiary center. The protocol comprised immediate subxiphoid decompression; insertion of two 16 Fr radiopaque Redon drains, placed anteriorly and posteriorly, each connected to a separate Drainobag bottle sustaining high negative pressure; hermetic layered closure; mechanical ventilation under sedation after decompression for at least 12 hours and progressive drain removal after 72 hours.
sections.results: All 4 patients achieved immediate hemodynamic recovery without conversion to emergency sternotomy. No hospital deaths or procedure-related complications occurred. No late pericardial reaccumulation, constrictive pericarditis or ventricular pseudoaneurysm occurred.
sections.conclusion: In this small single-center series, dual-drain subxiphoid drainage with continuous high-vacuum aspiration was feasible and associated with hemodynamic recovery without emergency sternotomy in 4 selected TAVI patients. Larger comparative studies are required before broader use can be recommended. These observations should be considered hypothesis-generating.Clinical ImpactCardiac tamponade during TAVI requires rapid, mechanism-directed treatment. Image-guided pericardiocentesis remains the usual first drainage step, whereas ongoing iatrogenic hemopericardium or failure to stabilize requires immediate surgical escalation. In 4 carefully selected patients, dual-drain subxiphoid decompression with continuous high-vacuum aspiration restored hemodynamic stability without emergency sternotomy. These findings support its feasibility as a rescue option in carefully selected cases, while larger comparative studies are needed to define its hemostatic effectiveness and its role relative to conventional drainage. Persistent bleeding or recurrent hemodynamic instability should prompt surgical conversion.

items.title: Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study.

sections.objective: CtDNA detection during adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) strongly associates with recurrence in oestrogen receptor (ER) positive early breast cancer (EBC), with potential to direct switches in adjuvant treatment.
sections.methods: TRAK-ER is a multicentre study for patients with high-risk, ER-positive, HER2-negative EBC, who undergo 3 monthly ctDNA surveillance for up to 3 years during adjuvant ET. High-risk included ≥4 involved lymph nodes; tumour >5 cm; 1-3 involved lymph nodes with additional high-risk features. Upon ctDNA detection, patients have staging scans and in the absence of radiological recurrence, are randomised to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard ET. ctDNA analysis was performed using a tumour informed assay (Labcorp). We report a protocol-specified analysis of ctDNA detection during surveillance, and results of contemporaneous radiological recurrence.
sections.results: 1133 patients were registered by September 2025, 928 had panels designed (design failed in 16.1% (178/1106), and 912 started ctDNA surveillance including results from 5810 tests (median 7 per patient). ctDNA detection rate was 5.0% (45/897) in the first test, and 1.3% (66/4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient level detection rate was 12.0% (109/912), with 1.1% (10/912) of patients having a clinical recurrence without prior ctDNA detection. Detection positively associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04) and negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative ctDNA detection rate at 5 years post-surgery was 23.7% (95%CI 14.5-31.9%). In patients with ctDNA detected on the first test, 65.9% (29/44) had radiological recurrence compared to 26.6% (17/64) in patients first detected on subsequent tests (P<0.001).
sections.conclusion: Results from TRAK-ER inform implementation of ctDNA surveillance in ER-positive EBC, including molecular relapse rates, factors associating with ctDNA detection and contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Ultrasensitive assays detecting ctDNA at low levels, are required to robustly identify patients prior to clinical recurrence. TRAK-ER is ongoing to assess the impact of treatment after molecular relapse detection.

items.title: Who Gets Feedback? Predictors of Receiving Narrative Feedback in Vascular Surgery Entrustable Professional Activities.

sections.objective: Surgical residents and fellows require high-quality feedback to guide skill development. Entrustable professional activity (EPA) assessments allow for frequent feedback in all phases of care. However, feedback is optional. We sought to understand predictors of feedback provision in a national, multi-institutional study of EPA assessments.
sections.methods: EPA assessments were collected in the multi-institutional Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. EPAs were rated on a scale of limited participation, direct supervision, indirect supervision and practice ready. Assessments included entrustment rating, postgraduate year (PGY), phase of care, and narrative feedback. Self-reported demographic information was collected. A mixed effects logistic regression was performed examining the effect of entrustment ratings, PGY, trainee and faculty gender and gender concordance, trainee underrepresented in medicine (URiM) identification, and phase of care on the probability of receiving narrative feedback.
sections.results: In total, 1,998 assessments were collected across 19 institutions (n=17 residencies, n=13 fellowships). Faculty submitted 983 assessments with 759 (77%) containing feedback. 58% of trainees were men, 54% white, and 65% of faculty were men. Phase of care, post-graduate year, faculty gender, trainee gender, faculty-trainee gender concordance, and URiM-identification were not associated with likelihood of feedback. However, higher entrustment ratings were associated with lower odds of receiving feedback (OR 2.76 [95% CI: 1.25-6.10]).
sections.conclusion: In this national, multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, demographic characteristics were not associated with likelihood of receiving or giving feedback. However, higher performing trainees are less likely to receive feedback. This may limit high-performing trainees' ability to reach their full potential.

items.title: Sex-Based Outcomes After Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a ten-year period in three stroke centers.
sections.methods: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within six months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite endpoint. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging (MRA-VWI).
sections.results: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs 23.5%, p=0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, p<0.01), HDL (56.8 ± 18.1 vs 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, p<0.01), and LDL (101.5 ± 45.4 vs 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, p<0.01); however, the LDL/HDL ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, p<0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs 48.6%, p=0.91), TIA (32.0% vs 33.5%, p=0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs 20.7%, p=0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs 4.0%, p=0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs 1.6%, p=0.61), TIA (0.7% vs 1.6%, p=0.23), MI (0.5% vs 0.0%, p=0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs 1.2%, p=0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs 24.3%, p=0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs 5.2%, p=0.32), TIA (5.1% vs 4.0%, p=0.50), MI (2.6% vs 3.6%, p=0.45), mortality (17.5% vs 19.1%, p=0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs 7.2%, p=0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs 4.8%, p=0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N=182), the 30-day (3.3% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs 31.9%, p=0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs 7.7%, p=0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs 6.6%, p=0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.
sections.conclusion: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a ten-year period at three high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.

items.title: Outcomes of single-branched TEVAR with cervical debranching for zone 0 and zone 1 aortic arch repair: A VQI analysis.

sections.objective: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).
sections.methods: The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
sections.results: Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. Mean age was 73.8±8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7±12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. Median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion Type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair.
sections.conclusion: Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.

items.title: Localization of Non-Compressible Torso Hemorrhage with Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound: A Swine Model.

sections.objective: Non-compressible torso hemorrhage (NCTH) remains a leading cause of preventable death in civilian and military trauma. In settings without cross-sectional imaging, the Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) is used to detect hemoperitoneum but is limited in evaluating the retroperitoneum, is highly operator dependent, and cannot reliably localize bleeding. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) has demonstrated high sensitivity for solid organ pathology, but its role in detecting and localizing NCTH is not well defined.
sections.methods: NCTH was induced in 18 swine (70-90 kg) via laparoscopic solid organ injury or endovascular injury to an aortic branch vessel. Standard FAST and CEUS were performed pre- and post-injury in a non-randomized, paired fashion. Outcomes included successful visualization of contrast extravasation with accurate localization of hemorrhage and time to hemorrhage detection.
sections.results: Both CEUS and FAST detected hemoperitoneum in all cases. CEUS identified active contrast extravasation from solid organ and vascular injuries in 78% of cases and improved detection of low-volume hemoperitoneum. CEUS also detected hemorrhage in the retroperitoneum. Time to detection was similar between modalities.
sections.conclusion: CEUS is a feasible adjunct to FAST for detecting and localizing NCTH. This swine model provides a reproducible platform for evaluating portable hemorrhage localization technologies in austere environments.

keywords: focused assessment with sonography for trauma

items.title: Fundus torsion in strabismus: measurement, clinical interpretation, and emerging imaging approaches.
items.abstract: Fundus torsion is an important but underused anatomical marker in strabismus evaluation, particularly for cyclovertical disorders. Unlike subjective cyclodeviation testing, fundus-based assessment provides an objective reference based on retinal landmarks, though it remains influenced by image acquisition, head position, ocular anatomy, and measurement conventions. We synthesize the anatomical basis of ocular and fundus torsion, contemporary qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, and disease-specific evidence across superior oblique palsy, pattern strabismus, pediatric and adult strabismus, and surgical follow-up. The review emphasizes 3 clinically important issues: the frequent dissociation between objective fundus torsion and subjective cyclodeviation, the need for method-specific interpretation using reproducibility and minimal-detectable-change data, and the importance of avoiding isolated treatment decisions based on anatomical torsion alone. Recent optical coherence tomography-based and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve measurement consistency and scalability, but current evidence supports their use as adjunctive tools rather than autonomous decision systems. Fundus torsion should therefore be interpreted within a multimodal clinical framework that integrates motility findings, sensory status, age, chronicity, fixation behavior, and surgical history. Treatment options include observation and symptom relief in selected patients, inferior oblique weakening for associated overaction, and torsion-directed surgery for persistent symptomatic excyclotorsion; comparative evidence remains limited. Prospective comparative treatment studies are a clinical research priority. Standardized acquisition protocols, explicit reporting conventions, age- and population-specific normative data, externally validated automated methods, and prospective studies linking torsional change to symptoms and functional outcomes are needed to strengthen the clinical utility of fundus torsion assessment.

items.title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: a competing-risk analysis.

sections.objective: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray's test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis.
sections.results: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P<.001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P<.001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P=.002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P=.030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 0.74-1.70), whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%.
sections.conclusion: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

items.title: Insulin Dependence Erodes the Cardiac and Survival Advantage of Asymptomatic Status After Carotid Revascularization.

sections.objective: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent (IDDM) and non-insulin-dependent DM (NIDDM) with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid artery stenting (CAS), stratified by symptom status.
sections.methods: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed January 2005-January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. Endpoints were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs).
sections.results: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) NIDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days there were 1,645 MIs, 2,051 ipsilateral strokes, 1,806 deaths, 3,626 strokes or deaths, and 5,029 MACE; at 1 year, 2,378, 2,924, 8,269, 10,750, and 12,646, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR 1.24), mortality (OR 1.19), and MACE (OR 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE OR 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P<0.001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR 1.54, P<0.001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR 1.05, P=0.41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR 1.19, P<0.001). Relative to CEA, TCAR and CAS were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR 2.10 and 1.93, respectively, P≤0.01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every endpoint.
sections.conclusion: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival endpoints, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable to symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

items.title: Femoral Artery Access Outcomes and Technical Considerations in Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome.

sections.objective: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures.
sections.methods: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access. Data were obtained from the global GEN-VEDS Natural History Study and a retrospective single center cohort. Demographics, genotype, procedural indication, access and closure techniques, access-related complications, and outcomes were abstracted from clinical record. Major access-related complications were defined as femoral artery dissection, pseudoaneurysm, rupture, or closure device failure requiring open operative repair.
sections.results: A total of 117 femoral artery access sites were used in 105 endovascular interventions among 60 patients between 1989 and 2025. Median age at intervention was 39 years, and 53.3% of patients were male. Among 99 procedures with known access modality, 84 were performed percutaneously and 15 involved planned open femoral exposure. Manual compression was used in 33 percutaneous access sites, with no major access-related complications. Percutaneous closure devices were used in 39 access sites; major complications occurred in 5 access sites across 5 procedures, all requiring unplanned surgical exposure and repair. One additional percutaneous access site required unplanned open repair for access-related arterial injury and external iliac artery dissection before any closure device was attempted. Of percutaneous closure device failures, Perclose ProGlide and Starclose had the highest rate of failure (18.8% and 33.3% respectively). Three of four affected patients had large amino acid substitutions or exon skip mutations; the remaining patient had a small amino acid substitution but underwent 16-Fr sheath placement. No access-related complications occurred after planned open exposure.
sections.conclusion: Femoral artery access in VEDS requires deliberate individualized planning. In this cohort, manual compression for smaller-caliber access (<6 Fr) was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas major complications occurred predominantly following attempted percutaneous closure. Planned open exposure, despite use in procedures involving larger sheath sizes, was not associated with access-related complications and may warrant consideration in selected circumstances, including procedures requiring larger sheath sizes, known prior closure-related arterial injury, and high-risk genotypes.

items.title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.

sections.objective: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly amid conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI.
sections.methods: We utilized the NIS (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. Our outcomes evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs. endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. Mann-Kendal trend tested monotonic temporal trends.
sections.results: An estimated 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations were included (mean age 69.7 years, 40.0% women, 69.5% White). Overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with reversal and steady rise thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations included revascularization (n=14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n=16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization decreased (ptrend=0.016), while endovascular remained stable (ptrend=0.368), and hospitalizations without revascularization increased (ptrend=0.016) over time. Endovascular revascularization rates did rise among females, non-frail patients, and those presenting with rest pain (all ptrend>0.05). Overall, in-hospital amputation (n=6,270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n=1,086 [2.3%]) remained stable (ptrend>0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased most substantially among hospitalizations without revascularization (ptrend=0.007).
sections.conclusion: We provide contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. Relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings underscore the need for further investigation into optimal CLTI patient selection and coordinated integration of non-operative care, such as medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

items.title: Autologous Anterior Lens Capsule as an Intrascleral Spacer in Deep Sclerectomy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: To compare deep sclerectomy (DS) combined with phacoemulsification (PE), with versus without an autologous anterior lens capsule spacer.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomized, parallel-group clinical trial. Sixty eyes of 60 adults with medically uncontrolled glaucoma and visually significant cataracts underwent PE-DS with an autologous anterior capsule spacer (Spacer group) or PE-DS alone (Control group). Follow-up was at least 12 months. The primary outcome was change in intraocular pressure (IOP) from baseline through 12 months. Secondary outcomes included glaucoma medication use, surgical success according to prespecified IOP-based criteria, and adverse events.
sections.results: Baseline IOP was similar (25.14 ± 9.62 vs 23.77 ± 5.18 mmHg) and both study groups had significant IOP reduction at all visits. IOP was significantly lower in the spacer group at month 6 (11.90 ± 1.82 vs 13.13 ± 2.20 mmHg; P = 0.022) and month 12 (12 ± 2.20 vs 13.29 ± 2.68 mmHg; P = 0.042). Medication use was lower in eyes with an autologous spacer at months 6 (0.14 ± 0.45 vs 0.48 ± 0.85; P= 0.063) and 12 (0.29 ± 0.66 vs 0.68 ± 1.04; P =0.094). Under stringent success definitions, survival favored the spacer (e.g., Definition C: IOP≤12 mmHg: 47.5% vs 15.5%; log-rank test P = 0.025).
sections.conclusion: Adding an autologous anterior capsule spacer during PE-DS was associated with lower IOP at 6 and 12 months and higher cumulative success under stringent IOP thresholds. Medication use was lower in the spacer group, although the between-group differences showed a trend toward statistical significance.

items.title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.

sections.objective: To determine the incidence of poor responsiveness to VEGF-A suppression in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) by evaluating the effect of continuous delivery of ranibizumab via the Port Delivery Platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in individual patients enrolled in the Pagoda clinical trial.
sections.methods: Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical trial data SUBJECTS: DME patients enrolled in Pagoda (NCT04108156). Change in central subfield thickness (CST) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over time was evaluated for the adjusted intent-to-treat (aITT) population in the Pagoda trial. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images obtained at each visit were analyzed for 56 PDS subjects from 8 sites to determine the time course of changes in intraretinal and subretinal fluid.
sections.results: In the aITT population the mean duration of follow up was 107.7 weeks in the PDS arm (n=272) and 100.7 weeks the IVT-PDS arm (n=238). The percentage of eyes with CST improvement into the normal range (≤325 µm) by the last visit was 87.9% in the PDS group and 85.3% in the IVT-PDS arm with mean time to normalization of 21.3 weeks and 20.6 weeks, respectively. All eyes in both arms showed reduction in CST over time although some exhibited periods of CST fluctuation and a few in each arm showed initial improvement followed by worsening at last follow up. In the eyes of 56 PDS patients that had detailed analysis of OCTs, normalization of CST occurred in 93% at a median of 17 weeks and elimination of intraretinal fluid in the central 1mm occurred in 84% at a median of 68 weeks. Only 3 of 56 eyes had poorly controlled DME at last follow up.
sections.conclusion: Sustained suppression of VEGF-A is sufficient to effectively treat DME in the vast majority of patients, but edema resolution may be slow in some patients giving the false impression of poor response to anti-VEGF-A treatment. In DME, the term unresponsive to anti-VEGF-A treatment should be replaced by slowly responsive.
sections.other: CST, BCVA, and time to resolution of edema.

items.title: Glioma regulates GABAergic signaling to drive hyperactivity and tumor progression.
items.abstract: Recent studies have identified bi-directional communication between neurons and glioma tumors as a key driver of hyperexcitability and malignant progression. Although much of this work has focused on the activity of excitatory neurons, the roles of inhibitory neurons remain poorly defined. Using in vivo screening approaches in autochthonous glioma models, we found that the loss of a γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (Slc6a1) enhanced glioma progression, promoted network hyperactivity, and influenced tonic GABA release by tumors. Mechanistically, we show that glioma tumors influence the activity of inhibitory neurons and that their subsequent stimulation suppresses tumor growth. Further screening of these phenomena identified diazepam binding inhibitor (DBI), a secreted negative allosteric modulator of GABA-A, as a link between glioma-related hyperexcitability and proliferation that functions through modulating inhibitory neuronal signaling. Collectively, our findings indicate that glioma tumors utilize multiple mechanisms to manipulate the activity of inhibitory neurons as a means to drive network hyperactivity, which ultimately facilitates malignant progression.

items.title: Trait-linked brainstem circuit resilience balances tau pathology-induced cellular vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Although tau pathology correlates with cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD), some individuals exhibit resilience by maintaining cognitive function. The mechanisms enabling this protection, particularly before widespread cortical degeneration occurs, remain elusive. Here, we identify a dynamic interplay between cellular vulnerability and circuit-level resilience that shapes cognitive outcomes in AD. Tau accumulation in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus (EW) impairs attention by inducing hypoexcitability in CART+ neurons via Kcnma1 upregulation, a vulnerability predictive of future decline in both 3×Tg-AD mice and AD patients. Conversely, a subset of AD mice with heightened exploratory behavior activates a compensatory medial parabrachial (mPB)-EW circuit, mediated by substance P-Tacr1 signaling, which sustains CART+ neuron function and delays cognitive deterioration. These findings reveal resilience as an active state enabled by trait-linked circuit plasticity that balances cellular vulnerability, defining multilevel targets for early intervention.

items.title: Natural Missplicing Events Amplified by an Elusive Deep-Intronic MYBPC3 Variant Cause Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Disruption of MYBPC3 precursor mRNA splicing is a frequent genetic cause of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Most often, it reflects changes at canonical sites or the creation of novel splice sites. Prediction tools usually prioritize splice variants with lower efficiency when they are distant from canonical sites. These elusive variants may explain HCM in patients considered genotype-negative after DNA testing.
sections.methods: Massively parallel sequencing identified the previously unreported deep-intronic variant MYBPC3 c.2308+227G>A in a cohort of genotype-negative patients with HCM from Salamanca, Spain. SpliceAI predicted a benign effect (Δ score, 0.03). However, its recurrent detection prompted us to conduct extensive analyses to investigate its pathogenicity, including genetic testing, clinical assessment, family studies, splicing assays, and haplotype reconstruction.
sections.results: We identified 35 unrelated HCM probands carrying c.2308+227G>A, plus 46 relatives from 27 families, yielding 81 confirmed carriers. Of these, 56 (69%) met diagnostic criteria for HCM (66% male; mean age, 53±15 years). By age 60 years, cumulative penetrance was estimated to be 81% in women and 96% in men. The combined logarithm of the odds score of 5.51 across 20 informative families provided strong evidence of cosegregation. During follow-up of probands, no significant differences were observed in heart failure, arrhythmic events, atrial fibrillation, or mortality when compared with cohorts carrying other pathogenic MYBPC3 variants. Blood splicing assays, confirmed in cardiac tissue, showed that c.2308+227G>A disrupts splicing by the use of pre-existing cryptic donor (c.2308+299) and acceptor (c.2309-580) splice sites, generating 2 misspliced mRNAs with partial intron retention or cryptic exon inclusion, which encode truncated proteins. These cryptic sites are the leading natural, unannotated missplicing events in intron 23, and some of the most frequent across the whole MYBPC3 precursor mRNA, as revealed by SpliceVault analysis of RNA sequencing databases. This deep-intronic variant does not alter essential splice motifs but promotes the use of pre-existing cryptic sites, likely through gain of splicing regulatory enhancer elements. The identification of a shared haplotype among HCM probands carrying this variant explains its recurrent detection, consistent with an ancient founder effect.
sections.conclusion: MYBPC3 c.2308+227G>A is a pathogenic splice-altering variant that causes HCM by amplifying natural missplicing events. These background splicing errors help explain how this elusive variant disrupts splicing without creating novel essential splice sites, thereby expanding the known mechanisms by which deep-intronic variants alter MYBPC3 splicing and ultimately contribute to HCM pathogenesis. Elusive MYBPC3 splice-altering variants should be considered in HCM patients with an unresolved genetic origin of disease.

items.title: Correlation Between EMS Agency Rates of Survival to Hospital Admission and Hospital Survival Outcomes for Cardiac Arrest.

sections.objective: Survival to hospital admission for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is an important resuscitation outcome to gauge emergency medical service (EMS) agency performance. However, its correlation with EMS rates of survival to hospital discharge and favorable neurological survival is unclear.
sections.methods: Using the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES), we identified adults with nontraumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrests during 2 periods: 2015 through 2019 (before the COVID-19 pandemic) and 2022 through 2024 (after the peak pandemic years). Multivariable hierarchical logistic regression was used to derive EMS agency-level risk-standardized survival rates for hospital admission, hospital discharge, and favorable neurological survival during each period. We then assessed the correlation between EMS agency rates of survival to admission versus discharge and favorable neurological survival using weighted linear regression, and whether the correlations differed by neighborhood income (above versus below median household income) and race and ethnicity (categorized as predominantly White [>80% of residents], majority Black or Hispanic [>50% of residents], or integrated).
sections.results: A total of 544 296 events from 1838 EMS agencies met inclusion criteria (252 137 pre-COVID; 292 159 post-COVID). During the period of 2015 to 2019, EMS rates of survival to admission were strongly correlated with survival to discharge (weighted r=0.68 [95% CI, 0.64-0.72]) and favorable neurological survival (weighted r=0.54 [95% CI, 0.43-0.59]). These correlations were similar during the period of 2022 through 2024 (weighted r=0.63 [95% CI, 0.59-0.66] and weighted r=0.48 [95% CI, 0.44-0.53], respectively). Neighborhood racial and ethnic composition modified the correlation between EMS rates of survival to admission and survival outcomes at discharge in both periods (all interactions <0.05), but the correlations remained strong in each neighborhood group. Similar findings were found for the interactions by neighborhood income strata.
