Using this method, we demonstrate the fabrication of metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V alongside, to our knowledge, the first single-crystal lattice structures containing complex zigzag ligaments, effectively eliminating theoretical size constraints for single-crystal components. The resulting bulk single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V exhibits an order-of-magnitude increase in creep resistance over standard grain-size scaling predictions, driven by the synergistic elimination of grain boundaries and an additive manufacturing-induced hierarchical α/β-architecture that regulates dislocation density, mobility and void evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the broad applicability of this technique by printing single crystals of hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. Our work introduces a large-scale method for single-crystal additive manufacturing, expanding the accessible materials library and enabling high-performance, complex geometries previously unattainable by classical methods.

items.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts.
items.abstract: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation1-5, rising tree mortality6-8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest9-11. Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions1-4,11,12. Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable1,9,13. Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts9,14-17. Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr-1, with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr-1) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011-2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr-1) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019-2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr-1) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr-1) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

items.title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis.
items.abstract: Anaerobic degradation of complex organic compounds to methane and carbon dioxide is common in the deep subsurface biosphere and has long been considered to require syntrophic cooperation, with methanogens confined to the terminal use of simple C1 and C2 substrates. Thermodynamic considerations, multi-omics analyses and microcosm experiments suggest that archaeal lineages are capable of methanogenic degradation of complex substrates1-6. However, experimental validation in pure culture was lacking. Here we report the isolation of a thermophilic archaeon, Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75, affiliated with Archaeoglobi, from a Chinese petroleum reservoir. Strain AA-75 not only converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, but also uses saturated fatty acids varying from C7:0 to C18:0 and unsaturated fatty acids including C16:1, C18:1 and C18:2 to produce methane. We term the latter lipotrophic methanogenesis, which integrates β-oxidation of fatty acids with the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway and the canonical methyl-tetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase complexes, together with an intracellular electron transfer system. A formaldehyde-methanol branch probably functions as an auxiliary route for C1 metabolism during methanogenesis. Methane produced from stearate is moderately 13C-enriched (δ13C-CH4 = -40.0‰ to -36.3‰), distinct from the strong 13C depletion characteristic of canonical methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that methanogens can function as primary degraders of complex organic matter, challenging the classical syntrophic paradigm and calling for refinement of current models of carbon cycling in the deep subsurface biosphere.

items.title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes.
items.abstract: Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A, a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase1,2. The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain3. Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A4,5 along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a-null mice and in human neurons6. Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome.

items.title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology.
items.abstract: The taxonomy and phylogeny of late Middle Pleistocene hominins in East Asia remain highly debated1. Xujiayao, a key representative assemblage with many fossils and a clear stratigraphy dating to around 199-138 thousand years ago, has been extensively studied, but its evolutionary position remains uncertain. Here, to clarify this, we analysed Xujiayao material through both palaeoproteomic analysis and morphological comparisons with other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo. Proteomic analysis of two specimens identified 18 endogenous proteins, and the Denisova-specific COL1A2-996 R>K mutation strongly supported their affiliation with the Denisovan lineage. Extended analysis identifies a set of shared morphological traits between Denisovan fossils (Xujiayao and Harbin) and other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo (such as Jinniushan, Dali and Hualongdong), indicating that they all belong to the Denisovan lineage. This analysis provides a comprehensive view of Denisovan features, showing both traits reminiscent of Homo erectus (such as a thick cranial vault) and those characteristic of modern humans (for example, a strongly arched temporal squama). They also share features with late Neanderthals, such as the structure of the temporal labyrinth and the presence of a suprainiac fossa. Notably, Denisovans are distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism.

items.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis.
items.abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species1-3, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2-BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington's disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

items.title: Zeolite-catalysed olefin carbonylation based on tuning spatial confinement.
items.abstract: Carbonylation is an important process used to produce aldehydes, carboxylic acids and esters1-5 that is usually catalysed by homogeneous metal complexes with ligands and iodide promoters6-12. Koch has reported that protons of mineral acids can also catalyse carbonylation13. Previous studies have demonstrated that Brønsted acidic zeolites can act as a heterogeneous, Koch-type catalyst for carbonylation of alcohols and olefins, but the products in this case are limited to tertiary carboxylic acids14-18. Here we show that targeted use of spatial confinement in a zeolite together with a high CO/olefin ratio can help break this limitation. We report that, with FER zeolite and a CO/olefin ratio of 360, olefin carbonylation can produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products; ethylene carbonylation to propanoic acid (PA) is achieved with 80% selectivity over 100 h and propylene carbonylation to isobutyric acid (IBA) is achieved with 95% selectivity over 750 h. The propylene and ethylene carbonylation selectivities decrease to 61% and 57%, respectively, as the CO/olefin ratio decreases to 24 and 90, respectively. Experiments in combination with theoretical calculations suggest that T2-O5 in eight-membered ring (8-MR) cavities of FER zeolite are the primary active sites for ethylene carbonylation and T3-O1 in ten-membered rings (10-MRs) are the primary active sites for propylene carbonylation. Our findings open new directions for olefin carbonylation and provide critical insights into the prerequisites for developing new zeolite-based carbonylation processes.

items.title: WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry.
items.abstract: WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint1-3. Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53-mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53-wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/CCDH1). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 (FZR1) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/CCDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

items.title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control.
items.abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2-7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

items.title: The contribution of salt marshes to wave attenuation during extreme storms.
items.abstract: Salt marshes protect coastlines by attenuating wind waves with their elevated marsh platform and above-ground vegetation1. Confidence in the persistence of this service under a changing climate requires knowledge on how extreme storms damage the platform and vegetation; however, a comprehensive, quantified understanding of salt marsh-wave interactions under extreme events is lacking. A unique experiment was conducted by transferring intact salt marsh to one of the world's largest wave flumes, and subsequently exposing it to increasingly higher waves that reach up to 2 m significant wave height. We show that marsh substrates can persist with negligible erosion, despite cumulative wave exposure. By contrast, the vegetation was progressively damaged during continued wave exposure, gradually reducing vegetation-related wave attenuation. Results emphasize that vegetation was most effective in attenuating waves at low-energy marsh coasts (up to 1 m), where attenuation exceeded 10% (up to 50%), whereas attenuation at high-energy marsh coasts (wave height > 1 m) does not exceed 10%. Our global assessment supports the differentiation between low- and high-energetic conditions resulting from the flume experiment. Our results suggest that the marsh platform remains stable under extreme wave events and that substantial wave attenuation by marsh vegetation is limited to low-energy marsh coasts.

items.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses.
items.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms-occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus-receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

items.title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits.
items.abstract: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes1,2. Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes3; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies4, we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51+ and CD51- astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51+ and CD51- astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51+ astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51+ astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51+ astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

items.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root.
items.abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory1. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

items.title: Touch-sensing digital pixel fibre enables interactive garment GUI.
items.abstract: Wearable computing promises to transform human interaction with information, yet conventional graphical user interfaces (GUIs) rely on planar, rigid displays incompatible with textiles, which are composed of one-dimensional fibres. Despite recent progress1,2 in flexible and fibre-based displays, bridging this fundamental dimensional mismatch remains challenging because existing approaches do not naturally provide the digitally addressable, high-throughput, information-rich interfaces required for interactive GUIs. Here we present a digital pixel fibre integrating addressable pixels, a common propagation-axis interconnection for scalable in-fibre circuitry and a coaxial sensing layer for fibre-level touch localization. Microelectronic components and a touch-gated resistive path system form a linear circuit that acts as both an interactive display backbone and a computational bus, while peripheral multimodal fibre sensors and actuators enable physiological, inertial, optical, and acoustic input and output. We integrate these fibres into the forearm portion of a garment sleeve to realize a GUI with a 96 × 54-pixel display, 30-frame-per-second refresh rate and 8-bit colour depth. It supports dynamic graphics, integrated audio-video playback, wireless data exchange and interactive computing functions, while maintaining the flexibility, washability, breathability and mechanical robustness of everyday textiles. By merging display, sensing and computation within a single fibre, this work establishes a scalable platform for intrinsically interactive textiles, opening pathways toward garments that operate as fully integrated computational systems.

items.title: Functional architecture of the human insula.
items.abstract: The insular cortex has a central role in pain1,2, interoception3,4 and feelings5,6, yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula7-10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal-posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral-posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior-polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

items.title: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).

sections.objective: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies.
sections.methods: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted.
sections.results: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24).
sections.conclusion: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice.
sections.other: 18 Dutch community hospitals. The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies.

items.title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts.
items.abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins.1-5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design6-8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts9. The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

items.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

items.title: Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival.
sections.methods: In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual.
sections.results: From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative.
sections.conclusion: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.

items.title: In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons.
items.abstract: Efficient integration of gene-length cargos in vivo remains challenging. Non-long terminal repeat (non-LTR) retrotransposons, which naturally mobilize large DNA segments through an RNA intermediate, could potentially address these limitations. Here, we developed a computational pipeline to systematically identify a diverse set of non-LTR retrotransposons. Extensive engineering generated elements capable of the efficient and stable insertion of reporter genes in human cells using RNA templates introduced in trans, which we term Gene Writers. Gene Writers successfully generated CD19 and CD20 chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cells ex vivo with robust antitumor activity. Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNA delivery enabled in vivo CAR-T cell generation and stable B cell depletion in a humanized mouse model. Our study delineates a comprehensive framework for the discovery, engineering, and application of non-LTR retrotransposons and demonstrates their utility for gene-sized cargo delivery in vivo, thereby bridging a critical gap in existing gene therapy modalities.

items.title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression.
items.abstract: Ferroptosis is implicated in multiple human diseases, but the lack of bioavailable inducers has limited its physiological study and therapeutic translation. Here, we report KY0418, a selective covalent inhibitor of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) featuring an isourea warhead, with high plasma stability and broad tissue distribution after oral dosing in mice. KY0418 specifically targets GPX4SeCys46 to induce ferroptosis hallmarks in human and mouse cancer cell lines, with greater selectivity than existing inhibitors. In a standardizable acute-liver-injury mouse model, KY0418 triggers ferroptotic ultrastructural changes matching those of established inducers, and systemic administration remodels tissue metabolism and generates hydroxyl radicals detectable by a chemiluminescent probe. Subcutaneous tumors from different cancers exhibited variable responses to KY0418 treatment, from no effect to about 70% growth inhibition, but KY0418 consistently eradicated circulating tumor cells and suppressed metastasis across multiple cancer models. These findings position KY0418 as a tool for advancing in vivo ferroptosis research and its clinical translation.

items.title: Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse.
items.abstract: T cell exhaustion limits the success of cancer immunotherapies, yet the proteomic changes underlying this dysfunctional state remain poorly understood. We integrated transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, turnover proteomics, and ubiquitin proteomics to construct a multi-omic atlas of T cell exhaustion. These studies identified pathways regulated through transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, including degradative and nondegradative ubiquitin modifications, and uncovered widespread changes in proteostasis, metabolism, and DNA repair. Major shifts were revealed in the ubiquitin-proteasome system, as differential expression of E3 ubiquitin ligases correlates with immunotherapy outcomes. These findings position the collapse of proteostasis as a central, underappreciated feature of T cell exhaustion and reveal opportunities to restore T cell function. We demonstrate that overexpression of the E3 ligase RNF166 enhances T cell persistence in vitro and in vivo. This work defines proteome-turnover dynamics as a critical regulatory layer in progressive T cell dysfunction, with broad implications for advancing cancer immunotherapy through manipulation of E3 ligases.

items.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula.
items.abstract: It has been unclear how Roman and later Germanic political control shaped the demography of Iberia and how it differed from other parts of Europe. We report genetic data from 243 ancient individuals dating to 100-800 CE, analyzed alongside 58 previously published individuals. In Roman times, we document an influx of people with ancestry from the Eastern Mediterranean and an influx of North Africans, especially in the center and south. Beginning in the 5th century, Germanic and Alan (Sarmatian) groups assumed political control. Although we identify individuals with Central-Northern European-associated ancestry, including siblings buried ∼725 km apart, the Hispano-Roman population remained continuous in Iberia. These demographic patterns contrast sharply with those in Britain, where major demographic change followed Rome's collapse, and with those in the central Mediterranean, where both periods were associated with profound transformations. Together, these findings highlight regional variation in admixture and continuity across post-Roman Europe.

items.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

sections.objective: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
sections.methods: In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results.
sections.results: A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

items.title: Hydrus microstent combined with cataract surgery or used alone: cost-utility analysis for UK.

sections.objective: Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) has the potential to become standard of care for patients with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), whether combined with cataract surgery (CS) or as a standalone procedure. This study provides evidence of cost-effectiveness for Hydrus Microstent for both indications in UK healthcare settings.
sections.methods: A cohort Markov model simulated the natural history of POAG to assess costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 15-year horizon, comparing Hydrus Microstent + CS with CS alone, and Hydrus Microstent to iStent standalone. Patient progression across glaucoma severity health states was modelled using a rate of progression (RoP) derived from 5-year visual field loss data in HORIZON trial (for mild to moderate POAG) and by trial-based annual number of medications from COMPARE trial (for moderate POAG), respectively. Conducted from the public healthcare payer perspective, model inputs were derived from UK publicly available sources and/or publications. Both deterministic and probabilistic analyses (PA) were performed.
sections.results: When compared with CS alone, Hydrus + CS was estimated to generate 0.334 more QALYs but £604 higher costs over the 15-year time horizon. When comparing Hydrus to iStent, Hydrus had £534 in projected savings and generated 0.068 more QALYs. The PA showed that the probability of Hydrus + CS being cost-effective compared to CS alone is 87.6%, and about 71.5% when compared to iStent. The results were consistent across scenario analyses.
sections.conclusion: Hydrus implantation is a cost-effective strategy both in combination with CS (for mild-to-moderate POAG) and as a standalone procedure (for moderate POAG) in UK healthcare settings.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
items.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

items.title: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy: A comprehensive review of clinical features, differential diagnosis, pathogenesis-related disease spectra, and management.
items.abstract: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy (PEHCR is a peripheral chorioretinopathy characterized by retinal pigment epithelium detachment with either blood, exudation, or both, and may present with macular hemorrhage, macular exudation, and vitreous hemorrhage. PEHCR exhibits a variety of features on fundus fluorescein angiography, indocyanine green angiography, and ultrasound examinations. The hemorrhagic type PEHCR may greatly resemble malignant melanoma, whereas the exudative type can mimics primary vitreoretinal lymphoma making differential diagnosis of great importance. The pathogenesis may involve choroidal neovascularization. Early studies suggested a link to age-related macular degeneration, while subsequent research has revealed a close association with polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy and pachychoroid disease spectrum. Most cases of PEHCR are self-limiting and may be observed alone. For those complicated by, or at risk of, macular exudation, macular hemorrhage, as well as vitreous hemorrhage, management strategies include intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections, vitrectomy, laser photocoagulation, photodynamic therapy, and cryotherapy.
keywords: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy

items.title: Subretinal fibrosis in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: From clinical features to fibrotic mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
items.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is a leading cause of irreversible central vision loss worldwide. Although intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy has substantially improved short-term outcomes, long-term vision is frequently limited by the development of subretinal fibrosis. This progressive scarring process occurs in a substantial proportion of patients and represents a major determinant of permanent visual impairment during long-term follow-up. Subretinal fibrosis arises from a complex interaction among structural injury, inflammatory signaling, and cellular reprogramming. Clinical and imaging characteristics are associated with fibrotic progression. Experimental studies have also provided insights into the underlying biological mechanisms. To organize heterogeneous evidence across clinical, cellular, and experimental studies, this review adopts a dual-axis framework as a working model for subretinal fibrosis in nAMD. The injury-inflammation axis describes processes that establish and maintain a persistent profibrotic microenvironment, whereas the cellular reprogramming axis describes phenotypic transitions of retinal and immune cell types, including epithelial-mesenchymal transition in retinal pigment epithelium cells, macrophage-to-myofibroblast transition, endothelial and pericyte plasticity, and glial remodeling, that may generate or contribute to extracellular matrix -producing effector cell populations. These axes' crosstalk through secretory signaling and matrix-dependent mechanical feedback may contribute to the persistence of fibrotic remodeling. Emerging therapeutic approaches include interventions targeting inflammatory pathways, fibrogenic signaling, and maladaptive cellular reprogramming, including transitions toward mesenchymal and matrix-producing phenotypes, as well as gene-based and bioengineered delivery strategies. This working model may help organize current evidence, identify unresolved causal links, and inform stage-specific therapeutic strategies.

items.title: A GABAergic preoptic-raphe circuit mediates paradoxical coupling of anxiety and social preference after comparative social deficit.
items.abstract: Social disconnection is a major risk factor for anxiety disorders, the most prevalent mental illnesses worldwide, yet its neural substrates remain unclear. Here, we establish a comparative social deficit (CSD) model in adult male mice that induces a paradoxical phenotype of increased anxiety-like behavior together with heightened social preference, a pattern conceptually similar to human loneliness. Mechanistically, CSD increases the excitability of medial preoptic GABAergic (mPOAGad2) neurons, which bidirectionally regulate CSD-induced behavioral changes. Transcriptomic and electrophysiological analyses identify downregulation of the Kv4.3 potassium channel (Kcnd3) as a molecular driver of mPOAGad2 hyperexcitability. Furthermore, mPOAGad2 neurons exert monosynaptic inhibition onto dorsal raphe serotonergic (DRN5-HT) neurons. This inhibitory projection, strengthened by CSD, mediates CSD-induced behavioral effects. These findings define a molecular and circuit mechanism by which social disconnection remodels mPOA-DRN interactions to drive the paradoxical coupling of anxiety and elevated social preference, providing a translational framework for understanding loneliness-related psychiatric vulnerability.

items.title: Approaches to Inferior Vena Cava Reconstruction in the Setting of Leiomyosarcoma.
items.abstract: IntroductionPrimary vascular leiomyosarcomas (PVLs) are rare, aggressive tumors arising from the smooth muscle cells of large veins, most commonly the inferior vena cava (IVC). Fewer than 500 cases have been reported worldwide, and outcomes remain poor without complete surgical resection. Treatment often requires complex venous and multivisceral reconstruction, but data on operative strategies and outcomes remain limited.MethodsWe reviewed four cases of IVC PVL resected at our institution between 2020 and 2023. Each case involved a distinct anatomic segment of the IVC, requiring individualized approaches to resection and vascular reconstruction.ResultsPatient 1 underwent infrarenal IVC resection with en bloc removal of bilateral renal veins and right renal artery, followed by complex reconstruction using cryopreserved cadaveric vein grafts to preserve bilateral renal function. Patients 2 and 3 presented with pararenal and suprarenal IVC tumors, respectively, and underwent en bloc resection with patch venoplasty using bovine pericardium, avoiding luminal narrowing and preserving caval flow. Patient 4 had a large pararenal IVC tumor with suprarenal atriocaval extension requiring cardiopulmonary bypass and patch venoplasty. She subsequently developed two recurrences, the second requiring thoracoabdominal exposure and interposition IVC bypass with a biologic tube graft. All patients recovered well postoperatively, with patent reconstructions and preserved organ function on surveillance imaging. At follow-up ranging from 12 months to 3 years, three patients remained disease-free, while one experienced recurrence managed with repeat resection.ConclusionsIVC leiomyosarcomas present unique surgical challenges requiring patient-specific operative strategies. Complete resection with negative margins remains the cornerstone of treatment, with vascular reconstruction essential to preserve renal function and venous return. This series contributes to the limited literature by demonstrating the feasibility of both standard (patch venoplasty) and complex (renal vein preservation, interposition grafting) reconstructions, highlighting the importance of individualized, multidisciplinary operative planning to optimize outcomes.

items.title: OCT to Assess Risk of Progression of Multiple Sclerosis: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

sections.objective: To review the current published literature on the utility of OCT of the retina in peripapillary and macular regions to predict or assess risk of disease activity in adult patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) and MS precursors (radiologically isolated syndrome and clinically isolated syndrome).
sections.methods: A literature search of the PubMed database was last performed in September 2025. Articles were limited to original research in the English language that included adult patients. The search yielded 275 articles that were examined in abstract form to exclude reviews, and 71 were reviewed in full text. Twenty-one articles were selected for inclusion in this assessment and were assigned a level of evidence rating by the panel methodologist.
sections.results: Two studies were rated level I, 8 studies were rated level II, and 11 studies were rated level III. Baseline measurements (lower thickness, faster thickness decline, and larger interocular thickness differences) of the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) and macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL) from OCT scans in patients with MS and precursors of MS were associated with future progression of MS as measured by disability, clinical relapses, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) changes. Multiple variable models support the independent association of OCT metrics and MS progression.
sections.conclusion: Evidence supports the development of OCT-derived pRNFL and macular GC-IPL thickness measurements as biomarkers for future progression of MS in patients with MS or MS precursor syndromes. Future work is needed to improve generalizability by studying demographically heterogeneous cohorts and should include determining the comparability of metrics obtained from different OCT manufacturers' hardware and software. Future research is also needed to guide interpretation of OCT in the context of other predictors of future disease activity such as MRI.
sections.other: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

items.title: Prostatic Artery Embolization in a Patient With Bilateral Internal Iliac Artery Occlusions.
items.abstract: Background: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an established treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia but can be challenging in complex anatomy. Study Sample: An 86-year-old male with history of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and aortobifemoral bypass presented with gross hematuria and urinary retention. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed BPH-related clot retention as the etiology. Careful review of preprocedural CT angiography revealed occluded bilateral internal iliac arteries, a right aberrant obturator artery (AOA) (corona mortis variant), arising from the inferior epigastric artery, which itself originated from the native right external iliac artery. The AOA supplied the entire prostate, perfusing both lobes and contributing to the contralateral pelvic circulation as well. Cone-beam CT and angiography confirmed the perfusion to both prostatic lobes. PAE was performed by accessing the native common femoral artery and selectively catheterizing the AOA. Embolization of the prostatic parenchyma was completed successfully while preserving flow to adjacent pelvic structures, avoiding non-target embolization. Results: The patient had complete resolution of hematuria and urinary retention and remained catheter-free at 1-year follow-up. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of pre-procedural evaluation and planning, demonstrating that PAE can be safely and effectively performed even in variant vascular anatomy.

items.title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

items.title: Tau-induced mitochondrial reverse electron transport drives neurodegeneration.
items.abstract: Hyperphosphorylation and aggregation of tau are pathological hallmarks of tauopathies. Mitochondrial dysfunction is also a common feature of tauopathies. The mechanistic link between tau abnormalities and mitochondrial dysfunction and its relationship to the physiological function of tau, however, is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that tau regulates mitochondrial reverse electron transport (RET), which produces excess reactive oxygen species (ROS), reduces the NAD+/NADH ratio, and is activated by aging or stress. In flies, mice, and human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neurons, tau depletion eliminates stress-induced RET and confers resilience. Mechanistically, tau enters mitochondria and directly interacts with the complex I subunit NDUFS3 to promote RET in a phosphorylation-dependent manner. Elevated RET further drives tau hyperphosphorylation, establishing a self-perpetuating pathological loop. Inhibition of RET ameliorates tau toxicity across species. RET regulation thus represents a previously unrecognized normal function of tau that becomes pathological in disease, providing a therapeutic target for various conditions characterized by tau abnormalities and mitochondrial dysfunction.

items.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells.
items.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics and safety of dolutegravir in term neonates exposed to HIV-1 (IMPAACT 2023): a phase 1, open-label, multicentre study.

sections.objective: Safe and effective antiretroviral options are needed for neonates exposed to HIV-1, but data supporting dolutegravir use from birth are scarce. The aim of this study was to evaluate dolutegravir pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability in term neonates, and to identify an appropriate dosing regimen.
sections.methods: IMPAACT 2023 was a phase 1, open-label, multicentre study conducted at 15 IMPAACT sites in South Africa, Thailand, and the USA from Oct 5, 2022, to May 22, 2025. Full-term neonates weighing at least 2 kg born to women living with HIV-1 were enrolled between birth and 5 days of life. In cohort 1, infants received two single dolutegravir doses using liquid suspension or 5 mg dispersible tablets. In cohort 2, infants received dolutegravir 5 mg every 48 h until day 14 of life, then every 24 h up to week 4-6 depending on duration of local standard-of-care antiretroviral prophylaxis. In both cohorts, participants were stratified by antepartum maternal dolutegravir exposure. Intensive pharmacokinetic sampling was done around each of the two single doses in cohort 1 and at 7 days post initial dose and at week 4 of life in cohort 2. Safety and tolerability were assessed up to week 16. Primary pharmacokinetic outcomes were the last observed concentration of dolutegravir after each dose and area under the observed single-dose concentration-time curve in cohort 1, and concentration of dolutegravir at the end of the dosing interval (Ctrough) and area under the concentration-time curve over one dosing interval (AUC0-τ) in cohort 2. Pharmacokinetic parameters were estimated by non-compartmental analysis in infants who received the dolutegravir dose under evaluation and had evaluable pharmacokinetic data from intensive sampling. Primary safety outcomes were study drug-related safety failure and safety failure from initial dosing up to 2 weeks after permanent study drug discontinuation. Safety outcomes were assessed in all infants who received at least one dose of dolutegravir and were summarised descriptively. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05406583, and is complete.
sections.results: Of 73 screened mother-infant pairs, 48 were enrolled between Oct 5, 2022, and Jan 21, 2025. All 48 infants started the study drug and were safety-evaluable; 41 were pharmacokinetic-evaluable. In cohort 1, concentration-time profiles showed prolonged elimination and wide interindividual variability, with substantial overlap between neonates with and without antepartum maternal dolutegravir exposure. In cohort 2, geometric mean Ctrough and AUC0-τ at the day 7 post initial dose visit were within target ranges. At week 4 of life, geometric mean AUC0-τ remained within target range, whereas Ctrough exceeded the target range but remained acceptable. No infants in either cohort had a study drug-related safety failure during the primary safety window. Safety failure occurred in zero of 18 infants in cohort 1 and four of 30 infants in cohort 2. Two of 48 infants had grade 1-2 adverse events that were considered related to dolutegravir.
sections.conclusion: These findings support dolutegravir as an option from birth for presumptive therapy or early treatment in term infants weighing at least 2 kg.

items.title: Sampling protein language models for functional protein design.
items.abstract: Protein language models have emerged as powerful tools for learning rich protein representations, improving tasks like structure prediction, mutation effect estimation, and homology detection. Their ability to model complex sequence distributions also holds promise for designing novel, functional proteins with applications in therapeutics, materials, and sustainability. Given the vastness of sequence space, efficient exploration is essential. However, most existing design approaches rely on single-mutant sampling strategies borrowed from natural language processing, which fail to capture epistatic interactions critical for function. Here, we develop an in silico framework to systematically compare sampling methods and introduce several approaches tailored for protein design. We show that sampling multiple mutations simultaneously substantially outperforms single-mutant approaches by better capturing epistatic effects. We evaluate these strategies across three protein families spanning eukaryotic, prokaryotic, and viral origins, examine key hyperparameters, and validate our findings on a de novo binder design task against a major therapeutic target.

items.title: Interstitial lung diseases in a changing climate: emerging risks and opportunities to improve care.
items.abstract: Although climate change represents one of the greatest public health challenges of our time, its impacts on patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unclear. This Personal View synthesises the evidence surrounding established, emerging, and postulated climate change health effects on patients with ILD, who are especially vulnerable to disease due to older age, reduced lung function, and sensitivity to inhaled exposures. Established risk factors for ILD such as air pollution might worsen with climate change, whereas other exposures such as extreme heat, viral illnesses, residential water intrusion, pollen, natural disasters, and desertification could pose novel threats to this population. Knowledge gaps exist across multiple domains, including wildfire smoke effects, the effects of climate on occupational ILD, and disaster preparedness. The incorporation of multiple research modalities, including patient-centred approaches, is crucial to address these gaps. Clinicians, scientists, and professional societies can lead climate-health research, the adoption of mitigation and adaptation strategies, and drive global policy actions to address this growing challenge.

items.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells.
items.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

items.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function.
items.abstract: The mechanisms by which hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) maintain long-term (LT) hematopoietic capacity and transition from quiescence remain incompletely understood, limiting their in vitro expansion and applications. Accumulating evidence underscores the importance of maintaining a low protein synthesis rate for HSC function, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified ribosome-associated proteins specifically enriched in HSCs and multipotent progenitors (MPPs) and found that RNA-binding protein gene with multiple splicing (Rbpms) is required for sustaining low protein synthesis rates in HSCs. Rbpms forms biomolecular condensates that sequester translation elongation factors and protein-folding chaperones from ribosomes, slowing translation elongation and ensuring proper protein folding in HSCs. Rbpms deletion led to accelerated protein synthesis, accumulation of misfolded proteins in HSCs, impaired LT hematopoietic reconstitution capacity, accompanied by aberrant exit from quiescence. Our findings unveil a unique mechanism of translation elongation regulation in HSCs and highlight significance of spatial compartmentalization and translational control in HSCs.

items.title: Effectiveness of a structured template to improve completeness of reporting randomised trial protocols: randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate whether providing authors with a manuscript template structured according to the Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials (SPIRIT) 2025 reporting guideline for use during revision improves the completeness of reporting in randomised trial protocols.
sections.methods: Randomised controlled trial. Handling editors asked the intervention group authors to use a SPIRIT based manuscript template when preparing their first revision. The template included structured subheadings corresponding to SPIRIT 2025 items, along with guidance on reporting. Editorial decisions were not conditional on use of the template. Control group manuscripts underwent standard peer review.
sections.results: Of the 70 manuscripts randomised (35 in each group), all were analysed, with no loss to follow-up. In the intervention group, completeness of reporting in randomised trial protocols improved by 0.61 points (95% confidence interval 0.20 to 1.01) compared with the control group, with mean (standard deviation) scores increasing from 5.42 (1.07) to 6.70 (1.23) and 5.77 (1.19) to 6.32 (0.94), respectively. The largest improvements were observed for recruitment, data collection methods, and access to data. Median time to submission of the first revision was similar between the intervention and control groups (27.10 v 29.86 days, respectively). Data on harms were not systematically collected. Among 14 of 35 survey respondents (40%), many (8/13, 62%) reported the template as time consuming and some (5/13, 39%) as burdensome. Most respondents, however, found it easy to use (10/13, 77%), helpful for improving the manuscript (9/13, 69%), and reassuring for adherence to SPIRIT (13/13, 100%).
sections.conclusion: Providing authors of randomised controlled trials with a SPIRIT based template during manuscript revision modestly improved the completeness of reporting in the trial protocols without extending revision times.
sections.other: BMJ Open. 70 of 74 manuscripts screened between 29 April and 27 May 2025 that reported randomised controlled trial protocols with a decision of minor or major revision after the first round of peer review were randomly allocated (1:1) using an R generated sequence. Authors were not informed of the study. The primary outcome was completeness of reporting score in the revised manuscript (adjusted for baseline), calculated as the mean of 11 SPIRIT items that are frequently inadequately reported (each scored 0, 0.5, or 1) and linearly rescaled to a 0-10 score. After submission of their first revision, authors in the intervention group completed an online survey. The survey included both fixed response and open ended questions designed to capture the authors' perceptions of ease of use, helpfulness, and any challenges encountered when using the template. Secondary outcomes included mean completeness of reporting scores for each item, median time to submission of the revised manuscript, and authors' experiences of using the template. Outcome assessors, but not editors or investigators, were masked.

items.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.
items.abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of QY201, an oral dual Janus kinase 1/tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor, in adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 dose-finding trial.

sections.objective: QY201 is a novel oral Janus kinase 1 and tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor. To evaluate the efficacy of multiple QY201 doses in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD), and to inform dose selection for phase 3 studies.
sections.methods: In this phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 200 adults with moderate-to-severe AD were randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive QY201 (5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg twice daily [BID]) or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving ≥75% improvement in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) at week 12.
sections.results: EASI-75 response rates at week 12 were 72.9%, 84.7% and 81.4% in the 5 mg BID, 10 mg BID, and 20 mg BID groups, respectively, compared with 18.5% in the placebo group (all P<0.0001). Investigator's Global Assessment response rates were 44.7% (P=0.0011), 64.3% (P<0.0001), and 71.3% (P<0.0001), respectively, versus 12.4% with placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 74.0%, 75.5%, and 90.4% of patients receiving QY201, compared to 69.4% with placebo; most were mild or moderate.
sections.conclusion: The phase 2 findings support further evaluation of QY201 at doses of 10 mg BID and 20 mg BID in confirmatory phase 3 trials.
sections.other: Short follow-up and single-country population.

items.title: Dyspnea during resting breathing and carbon dioxide rebreathing in adult patients with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.

sections.objective: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is an ultra-rare genetic disorder caused by PHOX2B mutations. Patients lack central CO2 chemosensitivity and require ventilatory support during sleep. Children with CCHS have been reported to lack CO2-induced air hunger, but respiratory sensations and dyspnea have not been characterized in adults.
sections.methods: This was a prospective controlled observational study conducted on a convenience sample derived from a national cohort of an ultrarare disease. Thirteen adult CCHS patients carrying PHOX2B mutations underwent Multidimensional Dyspnea Profile (MDP) assessment during unassisted resting breathing and at the end of CO2 rebreathing. Healthy controls were studied under the same conditions.
sections.results: Before the study, none of the patients had spontaneously reported dyspnea or bothersome respiratory sensations. When prompted with the MDP during resting breathing, 9/13 patients described breathing unpleasantness (non-zero MDP-A1) versus 0/18 controls (p < 0.0001), and 12/13 fulfilled criteria for dyspnea defined as breathing awareness associated with negative affect. During CO2 rebreathing, ventilatory responses remained profoundly blunted, yet breathing unpleasantness increased. Compared with controls, patients had lower sensory and affective ratings, with less frequent air hunger (p = 0.0108). MDP ratings did not correlate with ventilatory response to CO2 or genotype.
sections.conclusion: Adult CCHS patients can experience conscious unpleasant breathing awareness at rest and retain a perceptual response to CO2 despite abolished or nearly abolished central chemosensitivity. These findings suggest respiratory interoceptive pathways beyond canonical brainstem chemosensitive circuits and support active multidimensional assessment of dyspnea in adult CCHS patients.
sections.other: Do genetically characterized adult CCHS patients experience respiratory sensations and dyspnea during unassisted resting breathing and CO2 rebreathing, and along which dimensions?

items.title: Peritoneal dialysis induces hepatic metabolic stress as an instigator for systemic inflammation.

sections.objective: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is a lifesaving therapy in patients with kidney failure, but results in daily intraperitoneal glucose administration corresponding to 50% of the recommended energy intake, most of which enters the portal circulation.
