Structural analysis of the low ("trans") and high ("cis") efficacy states of AM-3 bound to the MOR reveals distinct binding modes, with each state driving unique ligand, receptor, and G protein dynamics. In mice, AM-3 drives reversible and repeatable optical control of antinociception across pain models with a reduced side effect profile owing to its limited brain accumulation and its ability to be locally activated.

items.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing.
items.abstract: Coleoid cephalopods exhibit the highest levels of adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADAR)-mediated RNA editing of any known taxon, yet the functional consequences of most recoding events remain unclear. Here, we integrated proteomics with biochemical and cellular assays to characterize recoding across the Doryteuthis pealeii proteome. This confirmed the translation of 7,997 recoded sites at the protein level and revealed how recoding reshapes the proteome by altering protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modifications, and enzymatic activity. We find that recoding also creates or ablates post-translational modification sites, with direct effects on protein function and protein-protein interactions. Recoding the E3 ligase MARCHF5 drives widespread changes in substrate ubiquitylation and perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis, illustrating how RNA editing can influence organelle function. Together, these data give a proteome-scale view of how extensive RNA recoding diversifies protein function in coleoid cephalopods and offer a framework for understanding how RNA-level plasticity shapes protein function and cellular physiology.

items.title: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation.
items.abstract: Self-organization generates cellular patterns that guide morphogenesis, but how it regulates collective cell fate remains underexplored. We show that cellular self-organization constrains the propagation of ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of oxidative cell death that can otherwise spread as unbounded trigger waves. The spatial patterning of cell density and alignment encodes transcriptional programs, priming cells toward ferroptosis-sensitive or -resistant fates. Low-density, misaligned regions with elevated YAP/TEAD1 activity are sensitive, whereas high-density, aligned regions with increased NRF2 expression form propagation-resistant boundaries. Cell elongation establishes a polarized distribution of oxidizable lipids, creating peroxidation hotspots at the cell poles that promote propagation along cell alignment. In silico and pharmacological perturbations reveal that pattern-dependent susceptibility and polarized lipid organization act together to constrain isotropic waves into spatially confined, anisotropic propagation. These findings identify self-organization as a systems-level mechanism governing collective homeostasis, providing a paradigm to explore how tissue-scale organization regulates cell death in development and disease.

items.title: Spatiotemporal co-transcriptomics uncovers coordinated rhizobia-legume stress programs supporting nitrogen fixation in Medicago.
items.abstract: Rhizobial nitrogen fixation in legume nodules requires precise spatial and temporal coordination between host and bacterial gene expression. Here, we applied spatial enhanced resolution omics sequencing (Stereo-seq) to profile Medicago nodules across five developmental stages, generating a co-transcriptomic atlas of nodule development. Using a mixed-probe capture strategy, we simultaneously detected host and rhizobial transcripts within the same tissue sections, enabling analysis of host-microbe transcriptional coordination during symbiosis. We identified dynamic changes in host cell composition and developmental trajectories and uncovered two transcription factors, MtERF82 and MtDOF53, required for maintenance of the indeterminate nodule meristem. Rhizobial and host genes exhibited stage- and zone-specific expression patterns along the nodule apex-to-base axis. Notably, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated stress responses in both host cells and rhizobia were linked to symbiotic nitrogen fixation. Functional analyses further showed that MtERF71 and MtCBF1 promote nitrogen fixation by regulating ROS homeostasis and activating key symbiotic genes, highlighting stress signaling as an integral component of mutualistic symbiosis.

items.title: A telomere-to-telomere map of somatic mutation burden and functional impact in a cancer.
items.abstract: Cancer genomes harbor extensive somatic genetic and epigenetic variation, yet large portions of the genome remain inaccessible to conventional reference-based analyses. Here, we demonstrate that pairing a near-telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) diploid assembly of a donor with deep short- and long-read sequencing of their melanoma reveals that 16% of somatic variants localize to sequences absent from GRCh38, with satellite repeats acting as hotspots for UV-associated mutagenesis. Centromere kinetochore binding domains emerge as focal sites of chromosome arm aneuploidy breakpoints and somatic genetic variation, features we further demonstrate are also present in non-cancerous tissues. By contrast, extensive epigenetic remodeling of kinetochore binding domains appears specific to oncogenesis. Single-molecule telomere analyses reconstruct the cycle of telomere erosion and telomerase-mediated extension during tumor evolution, while haplotype-resolved chromatin maps reveal widespread somatic epimutations impacting regulatory elements. Together, these findings define previously inaccessible dimensions of somatic variation and establish a framework for telomere-to-telomere studies of human mosaicism.

items.title: Somatic epimutations cap genetic determinism in the human diploid chromatin epigenome.
items.abstract: Diploid human cells contain two non-identical genomes, and differences in their regulation underlie human development and disease. We present Fiber-seq inferred regulatory elements (FIRE) and show that FIRE provides a more comprehensive and quantitative snapshot of the accessible chromatin landscape across the 6 Gbp diploid human genome, overcoming previously unrecognized biases in existing regulatory element catalogs. FIRE enables comprehensive detection of haplotype-selective chromatin accessibility (HSCA), exposing imprinted elements lacking underlying parent-of-origin differences in DNA methylation and gene regulatory modules that permit genes to escape X chromosome inactivation. We uncover that the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) locus harbors the most HSCA in immune cells, where we resolve specific transcription factor (TF) binding events disrupted by disease-associated variants. Finally, we demonstrate that the regulatory landscape of a cell is littered with autosomal somatic chromatin epimutations that are propagated by clonal expansions to create mitotically stable and non-genetically deterministic chromatin alterations.

items.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network.
items.abstract: Somatic mosaicism is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of human biology, yet the detection of somatic mutations remains challenging. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network conducted large-scale benchmarking experiments involving cell lines and donor tissues to evaluate sequencing technologies, experimental approaches, and computational methods for detecting different types of somatic mutations, generating community resources with >1,000× short-read and 100-400× long-read data for nine analyzed samples. We determined effective strategies for utilizing short- and long-read sequencing for mutation detection and demonstrated that using donor-specific and pangenome-inferred diploid assemblies improved calling, extending mutation catalogs to challenging genomic regions. We benchmarked six duplex technologies and showed that single-cell sequencing resolves cell-type-specific mutational patterns and heterogeneity. Our results indicate that bulk, single-cell, and duplex analyses are complementary and that leveraging all three provides comprehensive characterization of mosaicism within tissues. Together, these findings provide the scientific and clinical communities with a roadmap for accurate genome-wide somatic mutation analysis.
items.authors: Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues Network. Electronic address: abyzov.alexej@mayo.edu

items.title: Charting the silent variation within us.
items.abstract: Every cell in the human body carries its own genome, shaped by mutations acquired over a lifetime, yet this vast somatic variation has been nearly impossible to measure. The SMaHT Network now delivers benchmarked tools and the first body-wide map of somatic mosaicism, establishing a baseline of "normal" against which its roles in development, aging, and disease can finally be tested.

items.title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
items.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational capacity, analogous to scaling up parameters in machine learning models. By contrast, the steering subsystem (hypothalamus, pallidum, and brainstem) scales via diversification of bespoke cell types to encode innate drives and reflexes, functioning as a high-dimensional biological "reward function." This framework explains the divergence in how evolution has influenced these subsystems and offers a unified lens for understanding brain architecture and the etiology of brain disease; furthermore, it may inform model designs for artificial intelligence.

items.title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance.
items.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane-localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

items.title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine.
items.abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type-specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)-signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

items.title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe2/WS2 moiré superlattices.
items.abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe2/WS2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal-dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

items.title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions.
items.abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

items.title: Market dilution, fair use, and generative AI.
items.abstract: Market dilution theory, which could affect AI use in science, requires conceptual clarity and empirical evidence.

items.title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making.
items.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

items.title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators.
items.abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

items.title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions.
items.abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p-orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d-orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p-type WSe2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WOx, n-type WS2, and semimetallic WTe2. This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WOx/WSe2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide-semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

items.title: Adult Attention Deficit-Hyperactivity Disorder.
items.abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

items.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.

sections.objective: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges.
sections.methods: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point.
sections.results: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2).
sections.conclusion: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

items.title: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis.

sections.objective: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection.
sections.methods: We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Participants were assigned to receive icotrokinra at a once-daily dose of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 100 mg or placebo. The primary end point was clinical response at week 12. Secondary end points included clinical remission, remission of symptoms, and endoscopic improvement at week 12.
sections.results: A total of 252 participants underwent randomization: 63 were assigned to the 400-mg group, 62 to the 200-mg group, 64 to the 100-mg group, and 63 to the placebo group. All the doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo with respect to a clinical response at week 12, which occurred in 63% of the participants in the 400-mg group, 58% in the 200-mg group, and 55% in the 100-mg group, as compared with 27% in the placebo group (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants with clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher in the 400-mg group than in the placebo group (30% vs. 11%, P = 0.006), as were the percentage of participants with symptomatic remission (46% vs. 19%, P<0.001) and the percentage of participants with endoscopic improvement (37% vs. 14%, P = 0.002). Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 24% of the participants in the 200-mg group (P = 0.054 for the comparison with placebo); in accordance with the fixed-sequence testing procedure to account for multiple comparisons, no further formal testing of secondary end points was conducted. Through week 28, the percentage of participants with adverse events was 60% in the 400-mg group, 66% in the 200-mg group, 66% in the 100-mg group, and 62% in the placebo group. For serious adverse events, the percentages were 2%, 5%, 0%, and 10%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Among participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, a clinical response at week 12 was significantly more common with once-daily oral icotrokinra at each of three tested doses than with placebo. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; ANTHEM-UC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06049017.).

items.title: Ponatinib-Blinatumomab or Imatinib-Chemotherapy for Adult Ph-Positive ALL.

sections.objective: The outcome of Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-positive ALL) has greatly improved with the use of tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immunotherapy.
sections.methods: In this trial, we randomly assigned adult patients with Ph-positive ALL in a 2:1 ratio to receive ponatinib plus blinatumomab (intervention group) or imatinib plus chemotherapy (control group) as frontline treatment. A crossover to the intervention group was allowed for patients with persistence or reappearance of measurable residual disease in the control group. The primary end point was event-free survival.
sections.results: A total of 236 patients underwent randomization: 158 to the intervention group and 78 to the control group. The median age of the patients was 55 years (range, 24 to 82). At a median follow-up of 23.7 months, the estimated 24-month event-free survival was 86% in the intervention group and 67% in the control group (P<0.001). Survival with no measurable residual disease was 68% and 42%, respectively. At the end of induction, a complete hematologic response was observed in 94% of the patients in the intervention group and in 79% of those in the control group. After blinatumomab consolidation, a molecular response was observed in 71% and 49% of the patients, respectively. After crossover to the intervention group, 20 of 31 patients (64%) had a molecular response. Overall survival was 90% in the intervention group and 85% in the control group. The cumulative incidence of relapse was 5% and 13%, respectively. As of this report, only 19% of the patients in the intervention group had undergone hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after having had a first complete hematologic response.
sections.conclusion: In this phase 3 trial, a frontline chemotherapy-free targeted and immunotherapeutic approach was superior to the use of imatinib and chemotherapy. (Funded by Associazione Italiana per la Ricerca sul Cancro and others; GIMEMA ALL2820 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04722848.).

items.title: Immunoregulatory gene GIMAP6 suppresses lethal atherosclerotic vasculopathy and ischemic heart failure.
items.abstract: Controlling hyperlipidemia has reduced but not eliminated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) as a major cause of human mortality. Here, we report that loss of the immunoregulatory gene GTPase of immunity-associated protein 6 (Gimap6) in mice causes an inflammatory vasculopathy and accelerated atherosclerosis in the absence of hyperlipidemia. These vascular abnormalities cause progressive cardiac ischemia, myocardial infarction, and heart failure, culminating in early death. GIMAP6 loss precipitates early endothelial barrier failure and a mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS)-PPARγ-CD36 lipid-influx cascade that lowers the threshold for foam-cell formation and induces IL-6/MCP-1/TNF-mediated inflammation. Human hypomorphic GIMAP6 variants, including the African-ancestry-enriched V65I allele, are associated with altered monocyte redox balance, increased CD36-mediated lipid uptake, and early ASCVD. Thus, GIMAP6 is a crucial safeguard for vascular integrity that restrains endothelial dysfunction, macrophage foam cell generation, and inflammation that can cause lethal ASCVD independently of systemic hyperlipidemia.

items.title: Arabidopsis uses distinct coumarins and bacterial pathways for pH-adaptive iron acquisition.
items.abstract: Iron (Fe) limitation restricts plant growth in diverse soils, and root-associated microbes can alleviate plant Fe starvation. Whether plants integrate the edaphic environment and microbial activities into their Fe uptake strategies remains unclear. We show that bacterium-mediated alleviation of Fe deficiency in Arabidopsis functions at varying environmental pH and is taxonomically widespread among root microbiota isolates from soils with different edaphic profiles. This process is regulated by host-controlled and pH-adapted root exudation of different coumarin chemotypes. These exometabolites interact with root-associated bacteria to mobilize Fe either via bacterial siderophore-mediated chelation at circumneutral pH or redox-sensing-controlled, reduction-based pathways at acidic pH. The corresponding bacterial genes are prevalent in the root microbiota, and they likely evolved before the emergence of land plants. Our findings suggest that Fe malnutrition-induced exudation of redox-active metabolites by non-graminaceous plant species is a widespread adaptation for Fe mobilization from soil, mediated by the co-option of ancient microbial processes.

items.title: Lonvoguran Ziclumeran - In Vivo CRISPR Gene Editing in Hereditary Angioedema.

sections.objective: Hereditary angioedema is a rare and potentially life-threatening genetic condition characterized by recurrent and debilitating swelling attacks. Lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) - an investigational, in vivo gene-editing treatment based on clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) - is being developed as a single-dose treatment for hereditary angioedema.
sections.methods: In a phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, patients who were 16 years of age or older and had hereditary angioedema with C1 inhibitor deficiency to receive a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z (at a dose of 50 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the number of investigator-confirmed hereditary angioedema attacks per month (the monthly attack rate) from week 5 through week 28 after infusion.
sections.results: A total of 80 patients underwent randomization; 52 were assigned to receive lonvo-z and 28 to receive placebo. As of February 10, 2026, the median duration of follow-up was 7.5 months (range, 4.9 to 12.8). The least-squares mean monthly attack rate from weeks 5 through 28 was 0.26 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.45) in the lonvo-z group and 2.10 (95% CI, 1.55 to 2.86) in the placebo group (relative difference, -87%; 95% CI, -93 to -78; P 10% of the patients in the lonvo-z group) included infusion-related reaction, headache, fatigue, back pain, and upper respiratory tract infection. No serious or grade 3 or higher adverse events were reported in the lonvo-z group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with hereditary angioedema, a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z resulted in a significantly lower rate of hereditary angioedema attacks than placebo. (Funded by Intellia Therapeutics; HAELO ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06634420.).

items.title: Personalised ILM peeling for Myopic traction maculopathy.

sections.objective: To introduce a novel ILM peeling technique for S2 and S3 retinoschisis, termed 'Personalised ILM peeling', which selectively peels the ILM only within the schisis area while minimising postoperative complications.
sections.methods: 10 eyes from 9 patients with MRS underwent 'Personalised ILM peeling'. Preoperatively, the OCT radial scans, 3D Wide scans and retinal thickness map were comprehensively evaluated to delineate the extent of the schisis area and determine the specific region requiring ILM peel. Pre- and postoperative visual acuity, retinal thickness, including retinoschisis height, and visual field were analyzed.
sections.results: No case of recurrence were observed during a follow-up period exceeding 24 months. No Postoperative complications occurred in any of the 10 cases. Compared with preoperative measurements, postoperative visual acuity and retinal thickness, including retinoschisis height, demonstrated significant improvement.
sections.conclusion: Personalised ILM peeling is proposed as a novel, minimally invasive surgical approach for MRS. Many cases with high myopia are accompanied by visual field defects and it is expected that this will avoid damage to the fragile retina and nerve fibres.

items.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

sections.objective: Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue. To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.
sections.methods: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.
sections.results: Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).
sections.conclusion: Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.
sections.other: 15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS). Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

items.title: The effects of the arts and arts therapies on mental health outcomes of children and young people: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

sections.objective: There is growing evidence on the positive effects of the arts and arts therapies for mental health (MH) outcomes. This review aims to fill a research gap by establishing the evidence on the effects of arts-based interventions on selected MH outcomes for children and young people (CYP).
sections.methods: Our systematic review and meta-analysis included randomised controlled trials with CYP aged 5-24 years receiving any type of arts-based intervention. Five databases (CINAHL, Embase.com, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between 1/1/2005 and 18/5/2025. Two reviewers independently screened all records and assessed risk-of-bias using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB2) and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Data were initially extracted using the AI-assisted review tool Elicit and independently verified by two reviewers. All data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, and effect estimates for MH outcomes are summarised as Standardised Mean Differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic, with pre-specified subgroup and sensitivity analyses conducted to explore possible sources of inconsistency. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251015352).
sections.results: One hundred trials across 29 countries involving CYP aged 5-24 years with a range of health conditions, alongside healthy populations, were included in this review. Based on studies with some concerns or high risk-of-bias, arts-based interventions were found to reduce individuals' depression (1.06 SMD lower [95% CI 0.45-1.67, n = 1655, I 2 = 97%]), anxiety (0.75 SMD lower [95% CI 0.57-0.94, n = 3898, I 2 = 87%]), and increase individuals' wellbeing (0.53 SMD higher [95% CI 0.26-0.80, n = 538, I 2 = 49%]) and quality of life (0.54 SMD higher [95% CI 0.25-0.83, n = 441, I 2 = 53%]) on average post-intervention. Certainty of results relating to wellbeing and quality of life was low due to imprecision and concerns about risk of bias, and very low for depression and anxiety due to additional inconsistency associated with high heterogeneity. Findings relating to anxiety were further supported by biomarker data (blood pressure and heart rate) with moderate certainty.
sections.conclusion: This systematic review provides a comprehensive synthesis of evidence from randomised controlled trials assessing the effects of a wide variety arts-based interventions on the mental health of CYP. Although the strength of any conclusions is limited by heterogeneity, imprecision and bias of the studies assessed, average effects were similar to those typically reported for established non-arts-based psychosocial interventions, including talking therapies. These findings advance our understanding of arts-based therapeutic strategies for CYP's MH. Further high-quality trials, with larger sample sizes and standardised outcome measures and timepoints, are needed to improve the certainty of evidence in this area.

items.title: Association of Life's Essential 8 With Clonal Hematopoiesis and Coronary Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), characterized by clonal expansion of hematopoietic stem cells harboring preleukemic mutations, is an emerging cardiovascular disease risk factor. The American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score is the contemporary standard for quantifying cardiovascular health. However, the interplay between this novel genetic risk factor and classical health metrics remains unknown. This study sought to examine the association between LE8 score and CH prevalence, and determine their joint effects on incident coronary artery disease (CAD).
sections.methods: We analyzed 427,295 UK Biobank participants. Exposures included LE8 score and CH (evaluated as a composite and by common drivers: DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1). Associations with CH prevalence and incident CAD over a median 13.6-year follow-up were evaluated using multivariable regression.
sections.results: CH prevalence was 3.4%. A higher LE8 score was associated with significantly lower odds of CH and examined driver mutations, strongest for ASXL1 (OR: 0.79; 95% CI: 0.75-0.83; P < 0.001). CH significantly modified the protective effect of LE8 on CAD incidence on multiplicative and additive scales. A 1-SD increase in LE8 yielded an adjusted CAD HR of 0.74 (95% CI: 0.70-0.78) in CH carriers vs 0.68 (95% CI: 0.67-0.69) in noncarriers (Pinteraction = 0.005). Participants with ASXL1 CH subtype and low LE8 scores experienced the highest absolute CAD risk (18.7 vs 2.0 events/1,000 person-years in noncarriers with high LE8).
sections.conclusion: Optimal cardiovascular health is associated with a lower prevalence of CH. Although maintaining ideal cardiovascular health is associated with lower CAD risk in CH carriers, this protective benefit is attenuated compared with noncarriers.

items.title: Phenotype, treatment, and determinants of prognosis in Erdheim-Chester disease: an international, retrospective, cohort study.

sections.objective: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare histiocytosis driven by MAPK pathway gene mutations. Its clinical presentation is heterogeneous, and there is a shortage of data on natural history and prognosis. We aimed to characterise clinical presentation, associated conditions, treatments, outcomes, and determinants of prognosis in a large international Erdheim-Chester disease cohort.
sections.methods: We conducted an international, retrospective, cohort study of patients with biopsy-proven Erdheim-Chester disease diagnosed between Jan 1, 1985, and Dec 31, 2024. Data were collected in ten countries by participating investigators from referral centre records using standardised criteria, and were collected by participating investigators from referral centre records using standardised criteria. Patients with available data on treatment and outcome, and a minimum follow-up duration of 6 months, without excluding those who died before month 6, were included. Outcomes were response to treatment and overall survival. Mortality predictors were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression.
sections.results: From Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2025, we included 1174 patients (males 801 [68%], females 373 [32%]), whose median age at diagnosis was 58 (IQR 47-67) years. Multisystem disease (at least four organs) was present in 724 (62%) of 1174 patients, the most frequently affected sites being long bones (940 [80%] patients), retroperitoneum (742 [63%] patients), large vessels (540 [46%] patients), central nervous system (446 [38%] patients), and heart (412 [35%] patients). 643 (62%) of 1043 tested patients were BRAFV600E mutated, and 250 (36%) of 690 patients had clonal haematopoiesis. Overlap with other histiocytoses occurred in 161 (14%) of 1174 patients, whereas 321 (27%) patients had second cancer. First-line therapies most commonly included interferon-α (362 [34%] of 1057 patients) or targeted therapies (BRAF/MEK inhibitors 350 [33%] patients), with targeted therapies achieving the highest objective response rates (286 [74%] of 387 patients for BRAF inhibitors, and 185 [71%] of 262 patients for MEK inhibitors). After a median of 49 months (IQR 20-91), 261 (22%) patients died. Multivariable analysis identified older age (p<0·0001), neurodegeneration (HR 4·2, 95% CI 2·4-7·1; p<0·0001), high C-reactive protein (3·8, 1·6-9·1; p=0·0022), second haematological cancer (3·0, 1·5-6·0; p=0·0023), and no response to treatment (2·8, 1·6-5·1; p=0·0006) as independent predictors of mortality.
sections.conclusion: In a large Erdheim-Chester disease cohort spanning multiple eras, mortality remains substantial. These findings support early identification of patients with high-risk features and development of risk-adapted follow-up and treatment strategies.

items.title: Beyond Hemodynamics: Uremic Toxins, Post-Translational Modifications, and Inflammatory-Metabolic Remodeling in Uremic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Uremic cardiomyopathy has traditionally been attributed to pressure overload, volume overload, hypertension, and neurohormonal activation in chronic kidney disease. However, growing experimental and clinical evidence indicates that nonhemodynamic mechanisms also contribute to myocardial remodeling in uremia. These mechanisms include retention of uremic toxins and protein-bound solutes, mediators of mineral metabolism, gut-derived metabolites, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and post-translational protein modifications. In this review, we discuss uremic cardiomyopathy as a systemic inflammatory-metabolic disorder in which kidney failure reshapes myocardial structure and function through interacting biochemical and interorgan pathways. We first define the major classes of uremic toxins, including small water-soluble solutes, middle molecules, protein-bound uremic toxins, and reactive chemical intermediates. We then focus on post-translational modifications, particularly urea-derived cyanate-mediated carbamylation, a well-characterized uremia-associated mechanism that can alter collagen, extracellular matrix turnover, plasma proteins, lipoproteins, and potentially long-lived cardiac proteins. Additional injury pathways, including oxidative modifications, ferroptosis, fibroblast growth factor 23/Klotho imbalance, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation by indoxyl sulfate, gut-derived adrenergic metabolites, endotoxemia, and inflammasome signaling, are discussed as complementary and partially overlapping mechanisms. Because much of the current mechanistic evidence comes from preclinical models, circulating biomarkers, or associative human studies, we distinguish established evidence from plausible mechanistic hypotheses throughout the review. Finally, we discuss therapeutic implications, including enhanced toxin removal, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and future strategies targeting uremic toxins, proteostasis, ferroptosis, inflammasome activation, and toxin-induced post-translational modifications.

items.title: Improving clinical research through better use of clinical trial registry data.
items.abstract: Clinical trials are crucial for evidence generation on medicines. As of June, 2025, the European Union's (EU) clinical trial registries (Clinical Trial Information System and European Clinical Trial Register) housed data on nearly 55 000 clinical trials. The full potential of these data, especially when integrated with other sources such as real-world data, has remained mostly untapped for wider health-care innovation. In this Viewpoint, we report on the outcomes of an exploratory workshop with key stakeholders from across clinical research, held in Jan 25 and 26, 2024 under the Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) initiative. The workshop identified needs and potential use cases for the clinical trial registry data by gathering and analysing perspectives from diverse stakeholders. The analysis presented in this Viewpoint groups the use cases into three themes: optimising trial design and planning to leverage historical trial data for research optimisation; enhancing patient centricity to meet the diverse needs of patients; and strengthening the evaluation of evidence to maximise the collective effect of clinical trial data for regulatory, clinical, and policy decision making. Strong consensus emerged on key enablers for better use of data. These enablers were data standardisation to ensure consistent data representation among registries; data quality to enable reliable data analysis and decision making; interoperability to allow digital health systems to communicate seamlessly; and transparency to ensure data are made available to the public. As an initial step in addressing these needs, the European Medicines Agency developed the ACT EU trial map as a patient-oriented platform enabling easy trial discovery. The use cases identified at the workshop provide different starting points for supporting the setup of a clinical trial analytics ecosystem to enhance evidence-based decision making, foster innovation, guide funding, and ultimately benefit public health.

items.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.
sections.methods: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.
sections.results: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.
sections.conclusion: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

items.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks.
items.abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

items.title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation.
items.abstract: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology1,2. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes1,3,4. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

items.title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics.
items.abstract: The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis1-5. Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential6-10. Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell-transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

items.title: Bat-borne zoonoses: transmission, impact, prevention, and management.
items.abstract: Climate change and biodiversity loss are global environmental crises driving emerging infectious diseases, including bat-borne pathogens of public health significance: Ebola, Marburg, Nipah, Hendra, classic rabies virus, and Australian bat lyssavirus, as well as the fungus Histoplasma This review presents the evidence on the mechanisms of transmission, impact, and prevention and management strategies relevant to each of these pathogens. Transmission pathways vary between pathogens but often involve exposure to body fluids or excreta of a bat or other infected animal or human. The diseases associated with these infections have high mortality rates, and survivors may continue to experience a range of long term effects, including neurological and neuropsychiatric signs and symptoms. Prevention strategies may be implemented to reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover and human-to-human transmission of these pathogens, including better ecological stewardship, reducing exposure of domestic animals and humans to bats, isolation of infected people, and, where possible, vaccination of humans and animals. The mainstay of treatment for these conditions is supportive care; however, specific drugs are now available for histoplasmosis and Ebolavirus infection. In the face of climate change and further loss of biodiversity, developing more effective strategies to prevent and manage these conditions will be critical.

items.title: Evaluation of the accuracy, completeness, and compliance of current summary reporting of adverse events to the Food and Drug Administration using the manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database: cross sectional study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the accuracy and completeness of adverse event summary reports for medical devices and compliance of the reports with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requirements.
sections.methods: Cross sectional study. All adverse event summary reports filed in MAUDE from July 2019 to June 2025.
sections.results: 6308 summary reports were submitted to MAUDE containing 159 503 adverse events. Use of summary reports increased from 808 to 1757 between 2020 and 2024, a factor of 1.21 per year (P<0.001). Most (91%) adverse events in summary reports were for class 3 high risk devices. Summary reports lacked descriptions of potential device related problems: 57% of reports denoted an "adverse event without identified device or use problem" and 38% of reports selected "insufficient information" in the device problem code data field. Manufacturers incorrectly checked "N" (no) in the summary report (Y/N, reporting yes/no) field for 694 summary reports (11%) and erroneously listed "n=1" under the number of events field for 423 summary reports (7%), causing an undercount of 11 902 adverse events. The majority (55%) of summary reports failed to comply with the FDA reporting deadline of 30 days after the manufacturer became aware of the adverse event.
sections.conclusion: Adverse event summary reports in MAUDE are frequently incomplete, inaccurate, and delayed. Improvements are needed to ensure timely identification of device safety signals and uphold FDA transparency standards.
sections.other: The FDA manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database. Identification of device problem codes, appropriate identification as summary reports in the submission form, concordance between the number of events data field and the report narrative, and compliance with FDA reporting deadlines.

items.title: The Second and Third Decade After 103Pd Plaque Brachytherapy for Choroidal Melanoma.

sections.objective: To determine long-term visual and ocular outcomes in a large cohort of patients with choroidal melanoma treated using palladium-103 (103Pd) plaque brachytherapy.
sections.methods: This is a retrospective cohort study. 170 patients with a minimum of 10 years of continuous follow-up at The New York Eye Cancer Center following 103Pd plaque brachytherapy treatment for choroidal melanoma. The study includes collected data consisting of patient demographic characteristics, tumor features, such as size, location, and AJCC clinical T-category (cT), visual outcomes, variables related to post-treatment retinopathy management, and long-term ocular comorbidities.
sections.results: Among 170 patients with a minimum 10-year follow-up there was 100% local tumor control. One eye (0.6%) was enucleated due to neovascular glaucoma and patient choice. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated visual acuity retention rates of 92.7% at 12 years, 87.0% at 15 years, and 63.7% at 20 years defined as vision of 20/200 or better. Radiation retinopathy was managed with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, intravitreal corticosteroids, and laser treatment. Tumors located closer to the fovea were associated with increased foveal radiation doses and poorer visual acuity outcomes. Treatment of juxtapapillary and circumpapillary tumors was associated with the highest rates of vision loss.
sections.conclusion: This study is the largest and longest follow-up analysis of 103Pd plaque brachytherapy for choroidal melanoma. It provides new long-term information on tumor control, ocular morbidity, and visual outcomes that are valuable for patient counseling and therapeutic decision-making.
sections.other: The primary endpoints were tumor control, ocular conservation, and visual acuity. Secondary endpoints included long-term radiation-related complications, additional ocular interventions, and associated comorbidities. Statistical analyses were performed using the Kaplan-Meier survival method, t-tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, chi-square tests, and linear regression plots.

items.title: Iliac Vein Stenting With or Without Ovarian Vein Embolisation for May-Thurner Syndrome-Associated Pelvic Venous Disorder in Women: A Received-Treatment Retrospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: To compare clinical outcomes after iliac vein stenting (IVS) alone, simultaneous IVS plus ovarian vein embolisation (OVE), and staged IVS followed by OVE in women with May-Thurner syndrome-associated pelvic venous disorder.
sections.methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort study enrolled 184 women (aged 18-65 years) with imaging-confirmed MTS and haemodynamically significant PeVD at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital (January 2021-May 2025). The primary estimand was treatment received: IVS alone without subsequent OVE (Group A, n=71), simultaneous IVS plus OVE (Group B, n=54), or staged IVS then OVE (Group C, n=59, including 45 planned staged cases and 14 staged-after-IVS reassessment cases). The primary outcome was >=50% reduction in VAS pain score at 12 months. Confounding was addressed using multivariable regression, propensity score matching (PSM), stabilised inverse probability weighting (IPTW), overlap weighting, augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW), and repeated-measures models. OVE timing analyses were exploratory. Exact-date and time-updated OVE sensitivity analyses were performed, and available follow-up was extended through August 31, 2026.
sections.results: At 12 months, response rates were 54.9% for IVS alone, 74.1% for simultaneous IVS+OVE, and 69.5% for staged IVS+OVE (overall P=0.059). Receipt of OVE was associated with higher adjusted odds of response compared with IVS alone (adjusted OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.21-5.73; P=0.014), supported by IPTW (OR 3.12, bootstrap 95% CI 1.09-6.87). PSM (OR 2.60, 95% CI 0.93-7.29), overlap-weighted (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.66-8.84), and AIPW estimates were directionally consistent but imprecise. Planned staged and staged-after-IVS reassessment cases had 12-month response rates of 73.3% and 57.1%, respectively. Recorded 30-day events were mostly Grade I; one simultaneous IVS+OVE patient had Grade IIIa coil migration requiring snare retrieval, with no sequelae. Median follow-up was 37.3 months (IQR, 23.7-54.2; maximum, 66.5), with 96.6% stent patency among 29 patients assessed at 60 months.
sections.conclusion: In this received-treatment analysis, adjunctive OVE was associated with higher 12-month symptom-response rates compared with IVS alone. No statistically significant difference was observed between simultaneous and staged OVE, but this exploratory timing comparison should not be interpreted as equivalence. Because residual confounding remains and OVE adds procedure-specific events, these findings support selective consideration of OVE for patients with substantial ovarian vein reflux rather than routine incorporation for all patients.

items.title: Pharmacological strategies for the prevention and treatment of proliferative vitreoretinopathy: A comprehensive review.
items.abstract: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) represents the most significant complication and the primary cause of surgical failure in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair, occurring in approximately 5-10% of cases. The pathophysiology of PVR involves a counterproductive wound-healing response where retinal pigment epithelium and glial cells undergo dedifferentiation, migration, and proliferation. This process is largely driven by epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and a complex milieu of inflammatory mediators and growth factors, most notably platelet-derived growth factor and transforming growth factor beta. We investigate the evolving role of adjuvant pharmacotherapy in preventing and treating PVR. Traditional anti-inflammatory agents and anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapies have failed to demonstrate significant improvements in anatomical reattachment rates in human clinical trials. Conversely, anti-proliferative agents have shown more clinical potential; specifically, methotrexate has emerged as a leading candidate. Other promising strategies include the use of combined 5-fluorouracil and low molecular weight heparin, daunorubicin, and emerging biological therapies such as Rho Kinase and m-TOR inhibitors. Furthermore, innovative bio-functional polymers are being developed to modulate RNA transcription and suppress EMT factors. Therefore, PVR management is shifting toward a multimodal paradigm that integrates advanced surgical techniques with targeted molecular inhibition to improve functional success.

items.title: Spatial frequency domain imaging for assessment of skin fibrosis in systemic sclerosis: a prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Systemic sclerosis is an autoimmune disease with no approved skin-directed therapies. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) is the standard measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis, but it has limitations. There is an unmet need for a non-invasive skin outcome measure that is objective, biologically anchored to dermal fibrosis, and scalable for multicentre trials. We evaluated spatial frequency domain imaging (SFDI), a wide field, non-contact optical method as a systemic sclerosis skin outcome measure.
sections.methods: This single-centre, prospective, cohort study was done at the Division of Rheumatology at the Boston Medical Center (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with systemic sclerosis fulfilling the 2013 American College of Rheumatology-European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria. Control participants were people aged 18 years or older without autoimmune disease or known skin pathology. For all participants, exclusion criteria included skin malignancy, wounds or rashes at SFDI measurement sites (dorsal hands, forearms, and fingers). Participants in the pilot phase completed one study visit with SFDI, mRSS assessment, and optional forearm biopsy. In the expanded protocol phase, participants had a baseline visit, with follow-up visits once every 3 months during the first year and once every 6 months thereafter for 3 years. At each study visit, SFDI, high-frequency ultrasound, and durometry were done in all participants, and mRSS was assessed in patients with systemic sclerosis. Optional forearm biopsy and blood collection was done at baseline in consenting participants. Main analyses assessed baseline associations of SFDI parameters (diffuse reflectance [Rd] and reduced scattering coefficient [μs']) with mRSS and correlations with histological features of skin involvement in forearm biopsies (dermal fibrosis, collagen content, myofibroblast staining, epidermal and dermal thickness, and additional histological features). Linear mixed-effects models were used for associations and Spearman models for correlations. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were not involved in the study design.
sections.results: Between Oct 17, 2019, and June 18, 2025, 54 patients with systemic sclerosis and 30 healthy control participants were enrolled across the pilot and expanded protocol phases. The final analysis included 49 participants with systemic sclerosis and 25 control participants; biopsy samples were obtained from 34 participants with systemic sclerosis and 16 control participants. 38 (78%) of 49 participants with systemic sclerosis were female, 11 (22%) were male, 34 (69%) were White, and mean age was 50 years (SD 16). 20 (80%) of 25 control participants were female, five (20%) were male, 14 (56%) were White, and mean age was 49 years (SD 14). Rd and μs' were significantly lower in the systemic sclerosis cohort than in the control cohort across all mRSS strata, including sites where mRSS was 0. For each one-point increase in local mRSS there was a decrease in Rd (β=-0·0028, 95% CI -0·0050 to -0·0006; p=0·014) and μs' (β=-0·0158, 95% CI -0·0314 to -0·0003; p=0·047). SFDI correlations were weak to moderate with mRSS (r ranged from -0·38 to -0·48) and moderate with histological fibrosis (r ranged from -0·34 to -0·52).
sections.conclusion: SFDI provides an objective, non-invasive measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis that aligns with established clinical, imaging, and histological assessments. These findings support its potential as a quantitative outcome measure for evaluating skin disease in systemic sclerosis, consistent with Outcome Measures in Rheumatology principles.

items.title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.

sections.objective: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation.
sections.methods: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644.
sections.results: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p 7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis.
sections.conclusion: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication.

items.title: Strategies to develop therapeutic cancer vaccines for pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest malignancies. Conventional immunotherapies have shown little clinical benefit, largely due to the low neoantigenicity and profoundly immunosuppressive microenvironment of this cancer. Therapeutic cancer vaccines have emerged as a rational strategy to prime or amplify antitumour immunity, supported by advances in antigen discovery, genomic profiling, and vaccine engineering. Here, we report a review of clinical trials evaluating therapeutic cancer vaccines in PDAC. Eligible studies were identified through searches of ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to Aug 31, 2025, with manual screening of trial-linked publications up to Jan 31, 2026. 135 records were identified, of which 120 met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Across vaccine platforms-cell-based, nucleic acid-based, protein and peptide-based, microorganism-based, and multiplatform strategies-early-phase clinical studies consistently show feasibility, favourable safety profiles, and the induction of tumour-specific immune responses. However, immune activation has rarely translated into durable clinical benefit. To date, the most compelling biological signals derive from personalised neoantigen vaccines, particularly mRNA-based approaches, which can elicit high-magnitude CD8+ T-cell responses and long-lived clonal persistence in postoperative PDAC. Emerging evidence also supports the potential of shared neoantigens, such as KRASmut, as biologically relevant and scalable targets. Collectively, our findings highlight a shift towards rational vaccine combination strategies aimed at overcoming stromal and myeloid-mediated immunosuppression. Future progress will depend on integrating therapeutic vaccination into multimodal regimens and evaluating these approaches in adequately powered, biomarker-selected clinical trials.
